concepts.explanation: A solenoid produces a strong, nearly uniform magnetic field inside; polarity and magnitude depend on current and number of turns.

concepts.name: Forces between parallel currents
concepts.explanation: Parallel currents attract if they flow in the same direction and repel if in opposite directions.

concepts.name: Structure and operation of a transformer
concepts.explanation: Two coils linked by a magnetic core transfer energy by mutual induction; voltage ratio equals turns ratio in the ideal case.

concepts.name: Alternating current and voltage time variation
concepts.explanation: AC quantities vary periodically with time, typically sinusoidally, characterized by amplitude, period, and frequency.

concepts.name: Oscilloscope measurement of AC waveforms
concepts.explanation: Using an oscilloscope to display and measure AC signal properties such as amplitude, period, and frequency.

concepts.name: Effects of inductors on AC
concepts.explanation: Inductors oppose changes in current and influence AC circuits by introducing inductive reactance and energy storage in magnetic fields.

concepts.name: Uses of inductors
concepts.explanation: Applications of inductors in chokes, filters, and lighting circuits where they limit current and shape AC waveforms.

concepts.name: Verification of Joule’s law of heating
concepts.explanation: Experimental confirmation that heat produced in a conductor is proportional to I^2Rt, observable as temperature rise proportional to current squared.

concepts.name: Measurement of resistivity of a wire
concepts.explanation: Determining resistivity by measuring a wire’s resistance, length, and cross-sectional area and applying R = ρL/A.

concepts.name: Magnetic field of a permanent magnet
concepts.explanation: A permanent magnet produces a dipole magnetic field with lines emerging from the north pole and entering the south pole.

concepts.name: Experimental Investigation of Thermistor Resistance vs Temperature
concepts.explanation: Measure a thermistor’s resistance at various temperatures and plot the R–T relationship to observe how resistance changes with temperature.

concepts.name: Resistance–Temperature Characteristic of a Thermistor
concepts.explanation: The non-linear relationship between a thermistor’s resistance and temperature, typically showing decreasing resistance with increasing temperature.

concepts.name: Negative Temperature Coefficient (NTC) of Resistance
concepts.explanation: A property where a material’s resistance decreases as temperature increases, characteristic of many thermistors.

concepts.name: Plotting and Interpreting R–T Graphs for Thermistors
concepts.explanation: Graph resistance against temperature for a thermistor and interpret features such as sensitivity, linearity, and operating range.

concepts.name: Investigating I–V Characteristics Using Ammeter and Voltmeter
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to vary potential difference across a component, measure current with an ammeter and voltage with a voltmeter, plot I–V data, and control factors such as temperature and polarity (especially for diodes and electrolytes).

concepts.name: I–V Characteristics of a Metallic (Ohmic) Conductor
concepts.explanation: For a metal at constant temperature, current is proportional to potential difference, giving a straight-line I–V graph with constant resistance, exemplifying Ohm’s law.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristics of a Filament Lamp
concepts.explanation: A filament lamp exhibits a non-linear I–V curve because resistance increases with temperature as the filament heats, so current rises less rapidly at higher voltages.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristics of a Semiconductor Diode
concepts.explanation: A diode conducts significantly only in forward bias beyond a threshold (knee) voltage and shows very small current in reverse bias until breakdown, producing a highly non-linear, rectifying I–V curve.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristics of Copper Sulfate Solution with Copper Electrodes
concepts.explanation: In an electrolyte, current is carried by ions; the I–V relation can be approximately linear at low currents but is affected by electrolysis, electrode polarization, and ion concentration.

concepts.name: Determining Resistance from the Slope of an I–V Graph
concepts.explanation: For linear regions, resistance is obtained from the ratio ΔV/ΔI; for non-linear devices, dynamic (differential) resistance is found from the tangent slope at a point on the I–V curve.

concepts.name: Fraction Equivalence
concepts.explanation: Recognizing and generating equivalent fractions that represent the same quantity, and using visual models to justify equivalence.

concepts.name: Slope of a Line
concepts.explanation: Measuring the steepness of a line as rise over run and interpreting slope as a rate of change in linear relationships.

concepts.name: Area and Circumference of Circles
concepts.explanation: Using formulas C = 2πr and A = πr^2 to measure the boundary and interior of circles and solving related problems.

concepts.name: Scatter Plots and Line of Best Fit
concepts.explanation: Plotting paired data, identifying trends, and fitting a line to model and predict relationships between variables.

concepts.name: Function Concept
concepts.explanation: Viewing a function as a rule that assigns each input exactly one output and representing functions with tables, graphs, and equations.

concepts.name: Exponential Functions
concepts.explanation: Understanding growth and decay where quantities change by a constant factor per unit interval; interpreting y = ab^x.

concepts.name: The Electron
concepts.explanation: A fundamental negatively charged particle; carries the elementary charge and is central to atomic and electronic phenomena.

concepts.name: Photoelectric Effect
concepts.explanation: Emission of electrons from a metal surface when illuminated by light of frequency above a threshold; supports photon model with Kmax = hf − φ measured via stopping potential.

concepts.name: Thermionic Emission
concepts.explanation: Release of electrons from a heated metal when thermal energy overcomes the work function; foundational for vacuum tubes and electron guns.

concepts.name: X-rays: Production and Properties
concepts.explanation: X-rays are produced when high-speed electrons decelerate in a target (Bremsstrahlung) or via characteristic transitions; they are highly penetrating and ionizing.

concepts.name: Millikan Oil Drop Experiment
concepts.explanation: An experiment that determined the quantized elementary charge by balancing gravitational and electric forces on charged oil droplets.

concepts.name: Elementary Charge (e)
concepts.explanation: The smallest unit of electric charge, magnitude 1.602×10^-19 C; the electron has charge −e.

concepts.name: Cathode Ray Oscilloscope (CRO): Principles and Operation
concepts.explanation: Instrument that uses an electron beam deflected by electric fields to display voltage versus time; includes vertical input, time-base, and screen calibration.

concepts.name: Photoelectric Sensors
concepts.explanation: Devices that convert light into electrical signals using the photoelectric effect for detection and control applications (e.g., alarms, automatic doors).

concepts.name: Cathode Ray Tube: Electron Beam Production
concepts.explanation: Generation of a focused electron beam by thermionic emission and acceleration through a potential difference in a vacuum tube.

concepts.name: Deflection of Electron Beam in Electric Fields
concepts.explanation: Change in trajectory of an electron beam due to electric forces, used to measure charge-to-mass ratio and visualize field effects.

concepts.name: Deflection of Electron Beam in Magnetic Fields
concepts.explanation: Circular or helical motion of electrons under the Lorentz force in a magnetic field, relating radius to momentum and field strength.

concepts.name: Applications of X-rays in Medicine and Industry
concepts.explanation: Use of X-rays for imaging (radiography, CT), therapy, and non-destructive testing such as weld inspection and material analysis.

concepts.name: X-ray Hazards and Safety
concepts.explanation: Biological risks from ionizing radiation and associated protection principles: time, distance, and shielding.

concepts.name: Photocells in Optical Sound Track Reproduction
concepts.explanation: Use of photoelectric cells to convert varying light intensity on film sound tracks into electrical signals for audio playback.

concepts.name: Photocell Operation (Photoelectric Effect)
concepts.explanation: A photocell converts light into electric current by ejecting electrons from a photosensitive cathode when photons above a threshold frequency strike it; demonstrations measure photocurrent and stopping potential versus light intensity and frequency.

concepts.name: Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) Components and Operation
concepts.explanation: A vacuum tube with a thermionic cathode (electron gun), accelerating anodes, electrostatic or magnetic deflection, and a fluorescent screen to form, steer, and detect an electron beam.

concepts.name: Electron Volt (eV) as an Energy Unit
concepts.explanation: Energy gained by an electron accelerated through 1 volt (1 eV = 1.602×10^-19 J); larger scales include keV, MeV, and GeV commonly used in atomic, nuclear, and particle physics.

concepts.name: Elementary Charge
concepts.explanation: The smallest unit of free electric charge with magnitude e ≈ 1.602×10^-19 C; electrons carry −e and charge occurs in integer multiples of e.

concepts.name: Electron Mass and Position in the Atom
concepts.explanation: The electron has rest mass m_e ≈ 9.11×10^-31 kg and occupies regions around the nucleus (atomic orbitals), contributing little to atomic mass but defining atomic size and chemical behavior.

concepts.name: Photon Energy Relation E = hf
concepts.explanation: Each photon carries discrete energy proportional to its frequency, with E equal to Planck’s constant times frequency.

concepts.name: Effect of Light Frequency on Photoelectric Emission
concepts.explanation: Increasing frequency above the threshold increases the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons; below threshold no emission occurs.

concepts.name: Effect of Light Intensity on Photoelectric Emission
concepts.explanation: At fixed frequency above threshold, higher intensity increases photoelectric current (number of emitted electrons) but not their maximum kinetic energy.

concepts.name: Deflection of Cathode Rays in Electric and Magnetic Fields
concepts.explanation: Electron beams are deflected by electric and magnetic fields according to the Lorentz force, allowing control and measurement of beam trajectories.

concepts.name: Thermionic Emission from a Heated Filament
concepts.explanation: Electrons are emitted from a heated metal filament as thermal energy overcomes the work function, providing an electron source for tubes.

concepts.name: Cathode-Ray Tube Components and Functions
concepts.explanation: Heated filament (cathode) emits electrons, anode accelerates and directs the beam, and the fluorescent screen produces a visible spot.

concepts.name: Nature and properties of alpha, beta, and gamma radiation
concepts.explanation: Characterize alpha, beta, and gamma emissions by charge, mass, ionising ability, penetration power, and deflection in electric/magnetic fields.

concepts.name: Identification of alpha, beta, and gamma radiation by deflection and penetration
concepts.explanation: Use electric/magnetic field deflection, ionisation, and penetration tests to distinguish alpha, beta, and gamma radiation.

concepts.name: Half-life (T1/2) of a radioactive isotope
concepts.explanation: Define and apply half-life as the time for the number of undecayed nuclei or activity to reduce to half its initial value.

concepts.name: Balancing nuclear reactions using A and Z
concepts.explanation: Conserve mass number (A) and atomic number (Z) to write and interpret nuclear equations for decay and reactions.

concepts.name: Mass–energy equivalence in nuclear reactions (E = mc^2)
concepts.explanation: Relate mass defect to released or absorbed energy in nuclear processes using E = mc^2.

concepts.name: Principles of nuclear fission
concepts.explanation: Describe splitting of heavy nuclei into lighter nuclei with neutron emission and energy release; basis of chain reactions.

concepts.name: Principles of nuclear fusion and solar energy source
concepts.explanation: Explain fusion of light nuclei and its role as the Sun’s energy source via increased binding energy per nucleon.

concepts.name: Nuclear reactor components and functions
concepts.explanation: Identify fuel, moderator, control rods, and shielding and explain their roles in controlling fission in a reactor.

concepts.name: Rutherford scattering experiment and nuclear model
concepts.explanation: Outline alpha-particle scattering results leading to the model of a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.

concepts.name: Atomic nucleus composition: protons and neutrons
concepts.explanation: State that the nucleus consists of protons and neutrons; relate this to mass number and atomic number.

concepts.name: Nuclide notation and isotopes (A, Z, A_Z X)
concepts.explanation: Use nuclide notation to represent elements and define isotopes as nuclides with the same Z but different A.

concepts.name: Operation of a Geiger–Müller tube (detector of ionising radiation)
concepts.explanation: Explain how ionising radiation triggers gas amplification to produce detectable pulses counted as activity.

concepts.name: Becquerel (Bq) definition
concepts.explanation: Define the becquerel as the SI unit of activity equal to one disintegration per second.

concepts.name: Bohr model of the atom (descriptive)
concepts.explanation: Describe electrons in quantized orbits around the nucleus to account for discrete spectral lines.

concepts.name: Atomic energy levels
concepts.explanation: Explain that electrons occupy discrete energy states; transitions between levels involve photon emission or absorption.

concepts.name: Emission line spectra relation hf = E2 − E1
concepts.explanation: Relate emitted photon energy to the difference between atomic energy levels: hf equals E2 minus E1.

concepts.name: Hot-cathode X-ray tube: principle of operation
concepts.explanation: Describe thermionic emission, electron acceleration to a target, and X-ray generation in a vacuum tube.

concepts.name: Inverse photoelectric effect in X-ray production
concepts.explanation: Explain X-ray emission when high-energy electrons strike a target as the inverse of the photoelectric effect.

concepts.name: Properties of X-rays (EM waves, ionising, penetrating)
concepts.explanation: State that X-rays are electromagnetic waves with strong penetration and ionising capability.

concepts.name: Photocell (vacuum tube) structure and operation
concepts.explanation: Describe a photoelectric cell where illuminated cathode emits electrons, producing a current proportional to light intensity.

concepts.name: Health hazards of ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: Ionising radiation can damage biological tissue, increasing risks such as radiation sickness and cancer; the effect depends on radiation type, source activity, exposure time, and tissue sensitivity.

concepts.name: Radiation protection measures
concepts.explanation: Strategies to reduce exposure to ionising radiation using time minimization, distance maximization, shielding, and monitoring (e.g., badges), following ALARA principles.

concepts.name: Background radiation
concepts.explanation: The constant, low-level ionising radiation present in the environment from natural (cosmic rays, terrestrial sources like granite, radon) and artificial sources.

concepts.name: Measurement of background radiation
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to measure ambient count rate using a Geiger–Müller tube or other detector over fixed intervals, averaging over time and subtracting background from source measurements.

concepts.name: Activity of a radioactive source (Becquerel)
concepts.explanation: Activity is the number of nuclear decays per second, measured in becquerels (Bq), and indicates source strength relevant to exposure risk.

concepts.name: Types of ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: Alpha, beta, and gamma radiation differ in mass, charge, penetration, and ionising power, affecting detection methods, shielding, and biological impact.

concepts.name: Radon gas as a source of background radiation
concepts.explanation: Radon-222 from decay of uranium in rocks (e.g., granite) can accumulate indoors, significantly contributing to environmental dose and requiring ventilation or mitigation.

concepts.name: Medical and dental X-rays
concepts.explanation: Use of X-rays for imaging involves ionising radiation; risks are managed by justification, optimization of exposure, and shielding to protect patients and staff.

concepts.name: Disposal of nuclear waste
concepts.explanation: Safe management of radioactive waste using containment, shielding, and long-term storage matched to half-life to minimize environmental and biological hazards.

concepts.name: Newton's Second Law (F = ma)
concepts.explanation: The net force on a body is proportional to its acceleration and acts in the same direction; for constant mass, F = ma.

concepts.name: Equations of Motion (Constant Acceleration)
concepts.explanation: SUVAT kinematic relations connecting displacement, velocity, acceleration, and time for uniform acceleration.

concepts.name: Newton's Third Law
concepts.explanation: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction between interacting bodies.

concepts.name: Newton's First Law (Inertia)
concepts.explanation: A body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted on by a net external force.

concepts.name: Centripetal Force in Uniform Circular Motion
concepts.explanation: Inward force required for circular motion; for angular speed ω, F = m r ω^2.

concepts.name: Centripetal Acceleration (a = rω^2)
concepts.explanation: Radial acceleration of a body in uniform circular motion given by a = v^2/r = rω^2.

concepts.name: Angular Velocity and v = rω
concepts.explanation: Angular velocity ω describes rotation rate; for uniform circular motion, linear speed v equals rω.

concepts.name: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
concepts.explanation: Attractive force between two masses given by F = G m1 m2 / d^2.

concepts.name: Variation of g and Weight with Altitude
concepts.explanation: Gravitational field strength decreases with distance from Earth's center, reducing weight accordingly.

concepts.name: Orbital Period–Radius–Mass Relationship (Circular Orbits)
concepts.explanation: For circular satellite orbits, period depends on orbital radius and central mass via gravitational force–centripetal force balance.

concepts.name: Pressure in Liquids and Gases (Definition and Units)
concepts.explanation: Normal force per unit area, P = F/A, with applications to fluids.

concepts.name: Boyle's Law
concepts.explanation: For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume (PV = constant).

concepts.name: Archimedes' Principle
concepts.explanation: A body immersed in a fluid experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of fluid displaced.

concepts.name: Conditions for Equilibrium (ΣF = 0, Στ = 0)
concepts.explanation: A body is in equilibrium when the vector sum of forces is zero and the sum of moments about any point is zero.

concepts.name: Simple Harmonic Motion (Definition and Characteristics)
concepts.explanation: Periodic motion where acceleration is proportional to and directed toward the displacement from equilibrium.

concepts.name: Hooke's Law (F = kx)
concepts.explanation: Extension of an elastic spring is proportional to the applied force within the elastic limit.

concepts.name: Work Done by a Constant Force
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred by a force causing displacement in its direction: W = Fs (or W = F s cosθ).

concepts.name: Power (Rate of Doing Work)
concepts.explanation: Rate of energy transfer or work done per unit time, P = W/t (or P = Fv for constant speed).

concepts.name: Displacement (Definition and Units)
concepts.explanation: Vector measure of change in position with magnitude and direction, measured in meters.

concepts.name: Velocity (Definition and Units)
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of displacement with direction; measured in m/s.

concepts.name: Acceleration (Definition and Units)
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of velocity; measured in m/s^2.

concepts.name: Resolution of Coplanar Vectors
concepts.explanation: Breaking a vector into perpendicular components to simplify analysis of forces or motion.

concepts.name: Vector Addition of Perpendicular Vectors
concepts.explanation: Combining perpendicular vectors using the Pythagorean theorem and trigonometry to find resultants.

concepts.name: Velocity–Time Graphs (Interpretation)
concepts.explanation: Graphical analysis where slope gives acceleration and area under curve gives displacement.

concepts.name: Distance–Time Graphs (Interpretation)
concepts.explanation: Graphical analysis where slope gives speed; curvature indicates acceleration.

concepts.name: Demonstration of Newton's Laws with Low-Friction Track or Ticker-Tape
concepts.explanation: Procedures using air tracks or ticker-tape timers to verify relationships between force, mass, and acceleration.

concepts.name: Resultant Force Determination with Force Table/Newton Balances
concepts.explanation: Experimental composition of forces to find equilibrant or resultant using pulleys or balances.

concepts.name: Atmospheric Pressure (Collapsing-Can Demonstration)
concepts.explanation: Demonstration showing external air pressure exerting force on containers when internal pressure is reduced.

concepts.name: Density (ρ = m/V)
concepts.explanation: Mass per unit volume of a substance, typically measured in kg/m^3.

concepts.name: Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM)
concepts.explanation: Oscillatory motion where acceleration is proportional to and opposite the displacement, a = −ω^2 s; describes systems like springs and small-angle pendulums.

concepts.name: Hooke’s Law
concepts.explanation: The restoring force in an elastic system is proportional to displacement from equilibrium: F = −k s; defines the spring constant k.

concepts.name: Conservation of Energy
concepts.explanation: In a closed system, total energy remains constant while converting between forms such as kinetic and potential energy.

concepts.name: Kinetic Energy
concepts.explanation: Energy of motion given by Ek = 1/2 m v^2; depends on mass and the square of speed.

concepts.name: Gravitational Potential Energy
concepts.explanation: Energy due to position in a gravitational field near Earth: Ep = m g h.

concepts.name: Power
concepts.explanation: Rate of doing work or transferring energy: P = W/t; SI unit is the watt.

concepts.name: Efficiency (Percentage Efficiency)
concepts.explanation: Measure of energy or power conversion effectiveness: η = (Power output / Power input) × 100%.

concepts.name: Mechanical Work in One Dimension
concepts.explanation: Work done by a constant force parallel to displacement: W = F s; unit is the joule.

concepts.name: Simple Pendulum Period-Length Relationship
concepts.explanation: For small angles, the period T = 2π√(L/g); period depends on length L and gravitational acceleration g.

concepts.name: Measurement of g Using Simple Pendulum
concepts.explanation: Determine g by measuring T for various lengths L and using the slope of a T^2 vs L graph.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification that Acceleration Is Proportional to Force
concepts.explanation: Demonstrate Newton’s second law (a ∝ F for constant mass) using carts, masses, and sensors.

concepts.name: Principle of Conservation of Momentum
concepts.explanation: In an isolated system, total momentum remains constant before and after interactions.

concepts.name: Conservation of Momentum Verification
concepts.explanation: Experimentally test momentum conservation using low-friction tracks or trolleys and timing/light gates.

concepts.name: Investigation of Equilibrium of Coplanar Forces
concepts.explanation: Verify conditions for static equilibrium: ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0 for a rigid body under coplanar forces.

concepts.name: Verification of Boyle’s Law
concepts.explanation: Confirm the inverse relationship between pressure and volume (P ∝ 1/V) for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature.

concepts.name: Mass–Energy Equivalence
concepts.explanation: Mass is a form of energy related by E = m c^2; central to modern physics and nuclear processes.

concepts.name: Energy Conversion and Transfer
concepts.explanation: Real-world examples of energy changing forms, such as electrical to light/heat in bulbs or electrical to mechanical in motors.

concepts.name: Measurement of Velocity and Acceleration
concepts.explanation: Determine velocity and acceleration experimentally using timing devices, motion sensors, or light gates.

concepts.name: Estimating Average Power in Human Activity
concepts.explanation: Calculate average power output from stair climbing or repeated lifting using P = (work done)/time.

concepts.name: Demonstration of SHM Using Pendulum or Oscillating Magnet
concepts.explanation: Use a pendulum or magnet to illustrate periodic motion with restoring forces characteristic of SHM.

concepts.name: Period of a mass–spring oscillator
concepts.explanation: The period T of a mass m attached to a spring of constant k in simple harmonic motion is T = 2π√(m/k).

concepts.name: Angular frequency of simple harmonic motion
concepts.explanation: For a mass–spring system undergoing SHM, the angular frequency is ω = √(k/m).

concepts.name: Relation between period and angular frequency
concepts.explanation: For periodic motion, the period and angular frequency are related by T = 2π/ω.

concepts.name: Hooke's law for springs
concepts.explanation: The restoring force in a spring is proportional to its extension or compression: F = −k s.

concepts.name: Elastic potential energy in a spring
concepts.explanation: The energy stored in a stretched or compressed spring is U = 1/2 k s^2.

concepts.name: Determining spring constant from oscillation period
concepts.explanation: Measure the period T for various masses m, plot T^2 versus m, and use the slope 4π^2/k to find the spring constant k.

concepts.name: Fixed-Point Calibration (Ice and Steam Points)
concepts.explanation: Calibrating a thermometer by assigning 0°C at the ice point and 100°C at the steam point at standard atmospheric pressure, then graduating the scale between these points.

concepts.name: Comparing Thermometer Scales for an Unknown Temperature
concepts.explanation: Procedure to measure the same unknown temperature with two thermometers calibrated at fixed points to illustrate that different thermometric properties can yield different readings away from the fixed points.

concepts.name: Thermocouple Thermometry
concepts.explanation: Measurement of temperature using the electromotive force generated at the junction of two dissimilar metals, which varies with temperature.

concepts.name: Resistance Thermometer (RTD)
concepts.explanation: Temperature measurement based on the change in electrical resistance of a conductor or semiconductor with temperature.

concepts.name: Optical Pyrometer (Color-based Thermometry)
concepts.explanation: Non-contact temperature measurement by comparing the color or brightness of thermal radiation from a hot body to a calibrated source.

concepts.name: Linear Interpolation on Temperature Scales
concepts.explanation: Constructing a temperature scale by assuming a linear relationship between a thermometric property and temperature between two fixed points, using a straight-line graph to determine intermediate values.

concepts.name: Fixed Points for Temperature Calibration
concepts.explanation: Use of two reference points (e.g., defined fixed points) to calibrate a thermometer and anchor a temperature scale.

concepts.name: SI Unit of Temperature (Kelvin)
concepts.explanation: Kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature, defined from absolute zero and fixed physical constants.

concepts.name: Temperature (physical quantity)
concepts.explanation: A measure of the degree of hotness of a body; determines the direction of heat flow and is measured on scales such as kelvin and Celsius.

concepts.name: Triple Point of Water (as Temperature Reference)
concepts.explanation: The unique temperature and pressure where water’s solid, liquid, and vapor phases coexist; used as a fixed point in thermometry and historically to define the kelvin.

concepts.name: Temperature (Definition)
concepts.explanation: A physical quantity indicating the hotness or coldness of a body, defined operationally via thermometric properties and the kelvin scale.

concepts.name: Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics
concepts.explanation: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other; this underpins the definition and measurement of temperature.

concepts.name: Conversion between Celsius and Kelvin
concepts.explanation: Procedure to convert temperature values between scales using T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15 and θ(°C) = T(K) − 273.15.

concepts.name: Nonlinearity of Thermometers
concepts.explanation: Different thermometers can give different readings at the same temperature because the relationship between their thermometric property and true temperature is not perfectly linear.

concepts.name: Calibration of Thermometers (Fixed Points)
concepts.explanation: Setting a thermometer’s scale using agreed fixed points such as the ice point and steam point, and constructing a calibration curve to relate readings to temperature.

concepts.name: Ideal Gas Thermometer
concepts.explanation: A gas-based thermometer that approximates the thermodynamic temperature scale, used as a reference due to near-linear behavior at low pressure.

concepts.name: Measurement Uncertainty in Temperature Readings
concepts.explanation: Quantifying differences in temperature readings due to calibration, resolution, response time, and scale definition; reporting temperature with uncertainties.

concepts.name: Reference Thermometer (School Standard)
concepts.explanation: Use of a reliable commercial laboratory thermometer as the local standard instrument in a school lab to provide consistent temperature references.

concepts.name: Instrument Standardization in Temperature Measurement
concepts.explanation: Rationale and practice of adopting a standard thermometer to ensure accuracy, consistency, and comparability of temperature measurements across different instruments.

concepts.name: Multi-Digit Multiplication
concepts.explanation: Using place-value strategies and standard algorithms to multiply multi-digit whole numbers.
concepts.strand: Number and Operations in Base Ten

concepts.name: Ratio and Proportional Relationships
concepts.explanation: Using ratios to compare quantities and solving problems with unit rates and proportional relationships.

concepts.name: Similarity and Dilations
concepts.explanation: Understanding similarity transformations and using scale factors to solve geometric problems.

concepts.name: Descriptive Statistics
concepts.explanation: Summarizing data with mean, median, mode, and measures of spread, and interpreting distributions.

concepts.name: Conditional Probability
concepts.explanation: Calculating P(A|B) and using the multiplication rule to solve problems and assess independence.

concepts.name: Thermal Energy Change Equation (Q = mcΔT)
concepts.explanation: Calculates heat transferred to change a substance’s temperature without phase change using mass and specific heat capacity.

concepts.name: Relationship Between Heat Capacity and Specific Heat Capacity
concepts.explanation: Connects extensive and intensive properties via C = mc; distinguishes object-dependent heat capacity from material property c.

concepts.name: Experimental Determination of Specific Heat Capacity (Electrical Method)
concepts.explanation: Use an immersion heater and calorimeter; measure V, I, and t to get Q = VIt, record ΔT and mass m to compute c = Q/(mΔT), accounting for heat losses.

concepts.name: Method of Mixtures for Specific Heat Capacity
concepts.explanation: Determine c by mixing a hot sample with water in a calorimeter and applying conservation of energy to initial and final temperatures.

concepts.name: Specific Latent Heat of Fusion
concepts.explanation: Energy per unit mass needed to change a substance from solid to liquid (or vice versa) at its melting point without temperature change.

concepts.name: Specific Latent Heat of Vaporization
concepts.explanation: Energy per unit mass needed to change a substance from liquid to gas (or vice versa) at its boiling point without temperature change.

concepts.name: Heat
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred between systems due to a temperature difference; flows from higher to lower temperature and is measured in joules.

concepts.name: Heat Transfer
concepts.explanation: Transfer of thermal energy due to a temperature difference via conduction, convection, or radiation; frames how heat moves between systems.

concepts.name: Convection
concepts.explanation: Heat transfer by bulk motion of a fluid, including natural (buoyancy-driven) and forced convection; combines advection and diffusion of thermal energy.

concepts.name: Thermal Energy Storage
concepts.explanation: Retention of heat in a substance or system (e.g., sensible or latent storage) for later use; linked to material heat capacity and phase change.

concepts.name: Addition with Regrouping
concepts.explanation: Adding multi-digit numbers by composing a new ten or hundred when sums exceed 9 in a place.

concepts.name: Area and Perimeter of Rectangles
concepts.explanation: Calculating the space inside and the distance around rectangles using side lengths; connecting to arrays.

concepts.name: Order of Operations (PEMDAS)
concepts.explanation: Applying a conventional hierarchy to evaluate expressions with parentheses, exponents, multiplication/division, and addition/subtraction.

concepts.name: Slope and y-Intercept
concepts.explanation: Interpreting slope as rate of change and y-intercept as initial value in linear functions.

concepts.name: Triangle Similarity
concepts.explanation: Establishing when triangles have the same shape via AA, SSS, or SAS similarity and using scale factors.

concepts.name: Probability of Independent Events
concepts.explanation: Computing the chance of combined outcomes when events do not influence each other by multiplying probabilities.

concepts.name: Quadratic Functions in Vertex Form
concepts.explanation: Expressing y = a(x - h)^2 + k to reveal a parabola's vertex, direction, and stretch; supporting graphing and transformations.

concepts.name: Heat Pump (Refrigerator) Operation
concepts.explanation: A heat pump transfers heat from a colder region to a warmer region by doing external work; a refrigerator is a heat pump used for cooling via compression–condensation–expansion–evaporation cycle.

concepts.name: Coefficient of Performance (COP) of a Heat Pump
concepts.explanation: Efficiency metric of heat pumps: COP_heating = Q_hot/W_in and COP_cooling (refrigerator) = Q_cold/W_in; higher COP indicates less work for a given heat transfer.

concepts.name: U-Value (Thermal Transmittance)
concepts.explanation: Measure of heat flow through building elements per unit area per unit temperature difference (W m^-2 K^-1); lower U-values indicate better insulation.
concepts.broader_concept: Rate of Heat Transfer by Conduction

concepts.name: Heat Loss Calculation Using U-Values
concepts.explanation: Apply Q̇ = U A ΔT and E = U A ΔT t to estimate domestic heat loss through walls and windows and total energy over time.

concepts.name: Energy Required to Heat Water (Domestic Hot Water)
concepts.explanation: Use Q = m c ΔT to compute the energy needed to raise water temperature for domestic hot-water systems and assess efficiency.

concepts.name: Flat-Plate Solar Collector
concepts.explanation: A solar thermal device with a blackened absorber plate, transparent cover, insulation, and fluid-carrying tubes that converts solar radiation into heat for domestic hot water or space heating.

concepts.name: Surface Absorptivity and Emissivity in Thermal Radiation
concepts.explanation: Dark, matte surfaces absorb and emit thermal radiation more effectively than bright, shiny surfaces, influencing heating efficiency and solar energy collection.

concepts.name: Passive Solar Heating in Buildings
concepts.explanation: Use of building orientation, glazing, and thermal mass to capture and store solar energy for space heating without active mechanical systems.

concepts.name: Thermal Efficiency of Domestic Heating Systems
concepts.explanation: The ratio of useful heat output to energy input, typically expressed as a percentage, used to assess boilers, radiators, and solar heaters.

concepts.name: Convection Currents in Room Heating
concepts.explanation: Circulation of air where warm air rises from heaters and cool air sinks, distributing heat through the room.

concepts.name: Thermal Conductivity of Building Materials
concepts.explanation: A material property (k) determining the rate of heat conduction; lower values indicate better insulation and reduced heat loss in heating systems.

concepts.name: Specific Heat Capacity Calculations (Q = mcΔT)
concepts.explanation: Use Q = mcΔT to calculate the heat energy transferred, temperature change, or required mass during heating processes.

concepts.name: Simple Heating Experiment to Measure Specific Heat Capacity
concepts.explanation: Conduct a basic experiment by heating a known mass, measuring its temperature rise, and using c = Q/(mΔT) to estimate specific heat capacity.

concepts.name: Electrical Heating Energy Calculation (E = P × t)
concepts.explanation: Calculate the energy supplied by an electrical heater from its power rating and the heating time for use in thermal calculations.

concepts.name: Heat-Induced Temperature Rise
concepts.explanation: Adding heat to a body typically increases its temperature, with the amount of rise depending on the material and mass.

concepts.name: Sign Convention for Heat Transfer
concepts.explanation: Define heat added to a system as positive and heat removed as negative, consistent with observed temperature rise and fall.

concepts.name: Rate of Heat Conduction in Solids (Qualitative Factors)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative comparison of how fast heat flows through different solids based on material type, cross-sectional area, length, and temperature difference.

concepts.name: Thermal Conductivity of Solids: Definition and Units
concepts.explanation: A material property indicating how readily a solid conducts heat; defined via proportionality between heat flux and temperature gradient; units W m^-1 K^-1.

concepts.name: Temperature: Definition and Units
concepts.explanation: A measure of the thermal state of a body, related to average kinetic energy of particles; SI unit kelvin (K), commonly used scale Celsius (°C).

concepts.name: Measurement of Specific Heat Capacity
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of a substance's specific heat capacity by measuring temperature change for a known heat input and mass, typically via calorimetry or electrical heating, using c = Q/(mΔT).

concepts.name: Thermometer Calibration Curve
concepts.explanation: Establishing a calibration curve by comparing a thermometer’s readings to true temperatures provided by a standard mercury-in-glass thermometer to correct for scale nonlinearity and assign accurate temperature values.

concepts.name: Experimental Determination of the Specific Latent Heat of Fusion of Ice
concepts.explanation: Calorimetry procedure to determine L_f for ice by melting a known mass of ice in warmer water inside a calorimeter and using an energy balance to compute L_f.

concepts.name: Specific Latent Heat of Vaporization of Water
concepts.explanation: Energy required to convert 1 kg of liquid water at its boiling point into steam at the same temperature without temperature change; typically L_v ≈ 2.26e6 J/kg at 100°C. Related relation: Q = m L_v.

concepts.name: Multiplying Fractions
concepts.explanation: Using visual models and reasoning to multiply fractions and mixed numbers, and solving contextual problems.

concepts.name: Transformations in the Coordinate Plane
concepts.explanation: Describing and performing translations, reflections, rotations, and dilations to understand congruence and similarity.

concepts.name: Scatter Plots and Association
concepts.explanation: Creating scatter plots, describing trend, strength, and form, and informally fitting lines to model relationships.

concepts.name: Doppler Shift Calculations
concepts.explanation: Quantitative determination of frequency or wavelength shift using f' = f (v ± vo)/(v ∓ vs) for mechanical waves and Δλ/λ ≈ v/c for light.

concepts.name: Redshift of Stars
concepts.explanation: Increase in observed wavelength of starlight indicating recession of celestial objects, interpreted via the Doppler effect.

concepts.name: Doppler Radar Speed Measurement
concepts.explanation: Use of radio or microwave frequency shifts in reflected waves to determine vehicle speed in speed traps.

concepts.name: Ripple Tank Experiments
concepts.explanation: Experimental visualization of reflection, refraction, diffraction, and interference using water waves in a ripple tank.

concepts.name: Doppler Effect for Sound (Moving Source)
concepts.explanation: Change in the observed frequency of a sound wave due to motion of the source relative to a stationary observer; apply the Doppler formula to calculate frequency shift without deriving it (e.g., f' = f · v/(v ∓ v_s)).

concepts.name: Longitudinal vs Transverse Waves
concepts.explanation: Classification of mechanical waves by particle motion relative to wave propagation: longitudinal waves have particle oscillations parallel to the direction of travel, while transverse waves have perpendicular oscillations.

concepts.name: Wave Speed Equation (v = fλ)
concepts.explanation: Relationship linking wave speed v, frequency f, and wavelength λ; for electromagnetic waves in vacuum, v = c so c = fλ.

concepts.name: Wave Speed (Velocity)
concepts.explanation: Rate at which a wavefront or phase propagates through a medium, measured in m/s.

concepts.name: Stationary Waves (Standing Waves)
concepts.explanation: Wave pattern with fixed nodes and antinodes formed by superposition of two identical waves traveling in opposite directions.

concepts.name: Node Spacing and Wavelength in Standing Waves
concepts.explanation: In a standing wave, the distance between adjacent nodes equals half the wavelength, so λ = 2 × (inter-node distance).

concepts.name: Condition for Significant Diffraction (Aperture Size vs Wavelength)
concepts.explanation: Pronounced diffraction occurs when the aperture or obstacle size is comparable to the wavelength; diffraction is minimal when the size is much larger than the wavelength.

concepts.name: Single-Slit Diffraction (Qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Waves spread after passing through a narrow slit, producing a central maximum with subsidiary fringes; the degree of spreading increases as slit width approaches the wavelength.

concepts.name: Edge Diffraction at an Obstacle (Qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Waves bend around the edge of an obstacle, producing a transition from illuminated to shadowed regions whose sharpness depends on the wavelength relative to obstacle size.

concepts.name: Doppler Effect for a Moving Source and Stationary Observer
concepts.explanation: The observed frequency shifts when a wave source moves relative to a stationary observer; for a source speed vs in a medium with wave speed v, f' = f × v/(v ∓ vs) with sign depending on approach or recession.

concepts.name: Interference of Sound Waves
concepts.explanation: Superposition of coherent sound waves produces regions of constructive and destructive interference, leading to audible maxima and minima.

concepts.name: Resonance in Acoustic Systems
concepts.explanation: When a system is driven at one of its natural frequencies, energy transfer is maximized and large amplitude oscillations occur (resonance).

concepts.name: Standing Waves and Harmonics in Strings and Pipes
concepts.explanation: Nodes and antinodes form standing wave patterns in stretched strings and air columns; boundary conditions set the fundamental frequency and harmonic series (open: L = nλ/2, closed: L = (2n−1)λ/4).

concepts.name: Frequency and Pitch
concepts.explanation: Perceived pitch increases with the frequency of a sound wave; musical notes correspond to specific frequencies.

concepts.name: Amplitude and Loudness
concepts.explanation: Greater wave amplitude corresponds to higher intensity, while perceived loudness increases roughly logarithmically with intensity.

concepts.name: Speed of Sound in Different Media
concepts.explanation: The speed of sound depends on the medium’s elastic properties and density, increasing in solids and with temperature in gases.

concepts.name: Noise Reduction by Destructive Interference
concepts.explanation: Active noise control uses a phase-inverted sound to cancel unwanted noise via destructive interference.

concepts.name: Measuring Sound Level with a Sound-Level Meter
concepts.explanation: Use a calibrated meter (often A-weighted) to measure and report sound intensity level in decibels.

concepts.name: Two-Loudspeaker Interference Experiment
concepts.explanation: Using a signal generator and two coherent loudspeakers, map loud and quiet regions to demonstrate interference and determine wavelength.

concepts.name: Demonstrating Sound Requires a Medium (Bell-Jar Experiment)
concepts.explanation: An alarm inside a bell jar becomes inaudible as air is evacuated, showing sound cannot travel in vacuum.

concepts.name: Tuning Fork Resonance Demonstration
concepts.explanation: A tuning fork excites large-amplitude vibrations in a matching resonance box or in another identical fork, illustrating resonance at the natural frequency.

concepts.name: Standing Waves in Strings
concepts.explanation: Formation of stationary wave patterns on a stretched string with nodes and antinodes, determining allowed modes and fundamental frequency.

concepts.name: Stretched String Frequency Formula
concepts.explanation: The fundamental frequency of a stretched string is f = (1/2L) sqrt(T/μ), where L is length, T is tension, and μ is linear mass density.

concepts.name: Harmonics in Strings and Pipes
concepts.explanation: Discrete overtone series arising from standing waves; integer multiples of the fundamental for strings and open pipes, with only odd harmonics in closed pipes.

concepts.name: Standing Waves in Air Columns (Pipes)
concepts.explanation: Resonant standing waves in open and closed pipes, with frequency determined by boundary conditions and pipe length.

concepts.name: Sound Intensity
concepts.explanation: Acoustic power per unit area (W m^-2); definition and SI unit for quantifying sound energy flow.

concepts.name: 3 dB Rule for Doubling Intensity
concepts.explanation: A doubling of sound intensity increases the sound intensity level by approximately 3 dB.

concepts.name: A-weighted Decibel Scale dB(A)
concepts.explanation: Frequency-weighted decibel scale approximating human ear sensitivity, used for practical noise measurements.

concepts.name: Measurement of the Speed of Sound in Air
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of sound speed using timing, resonance, or interference methods in air.

concepts.name: Investigation of Fundamental Frequency vs Length for a Stretched String
concepts.explanation: Laboratory study showing the inverse relationship f ∝ 1/L by measuring how fundamental frequency changes with string length.

concepts.name: Investigation of Fundamental Frequency vs Tension for a Stretched String
concepts.explanation: Laboratory study showing f ∝ sqrt(T) by measuring how the fundamental frequency varies with string tension.

concepts.name: Laws of Refraction (Snell’s Law)
concepts.explanation: Relates angles of incidence and refraction across a boundary by n1 sin i = n2 sin r; incident ray, refracted ray, and normal are coplanar and paths are reversible.

concepts.name: Refractive Index from Relative Speeds
concepts.explanation: Defines refractive index as n = c/v and relative index n21 = v1/v2, linking optical density to wave speed and to Snell’s law.

concepts.name: Linear Magnification Formula
concepts.explanation: Defines magnification as m = v/u = image height/object height; sign indicates image orientation.

concepts.name: Image Formation by Plane and Spherical Mirrors
concepts.explanation: Describes image characteristics (real/virtual, upright/inverted, magnification, laterality) for plane, concave, and convex mirrors using ray diagrams or formulae.

concepts.name: Optical Fibre Transmission via Total Internal Reflection
concepts.explanation: Guides light in a high-index core by total internal reflection at the core–cladding boundary; foundational to telecommunications and endoscopy.

concepts.name: Prism Reflectors Using Total Internal Reflection
concepts.explanation: Right-angle prisms use TIR to redirect or invert light paths with high efficiency, used in devices like periscopes and binoculars.

concepts.name: Mirage Formation by Refraction in a Non-Uniform Medium
concepts.explanation: Temperature-induced refractive index gradients bend light, producing inferior or superior mirages observed on roads or over water.

concepts.name: Uses of Concave and Convex Mirrors
concepts.explanation: Applies mirror image properties: concave mirrors for illumination/examination (dentists, projectors), convex mirrors for wide field of view (driving, security).

concepts.name: Corrective Lenses in Spectacles
concepts.explanation: Converging and diverging lenses adjust optical power to correct myopia and hyperopia, analyzed with the thin lens equation.

concepts.name: Retroreflection in Road Signs
concepts.explanation: Microprismatic or glass-bead structures return incident light toward the source via refraction and total internal reflection to enhance visibility.

concepts.name: Thin Lens Equation (1/f = 1/u + 1/v)
concepts.explanation: Relates focal length f, object distance u, and image distance v for a single thin lens; foundation for predicting image position.

concepts.name: Linear Magnification of a Lens (m = v/u)
concepts.explanation: Defines image magnification as the ratio of image distance to object distance; connects to image size relative to object size.

concepts.name: Power of a Lens (P = 1/f)
concepts.explanation: Defines optical power P in dioptres as the reciprocal of focal length f in meters; measures a lens’s converging or diverging strength.

concepts.name: Equivalent Power of Lenses in Contact (P = P1 + P2)
concepts.explanation: For thin lenses placed in contact, the total optical power equals the sum of individual powers, enabling design of compound lenses.

concepts.name: Focal Length of a Thin Lens
concepts.explanation: The distance from the lens to its focal point where parallel rays converge (or appear to diverge); fundamental parameter governing image formation and power.

concepts.name: Light Transmission in Optical Fibres via Total Internal Reflection
concepts.explanation: Guiding of light within a higher-index core surrounded by lower-index cladding when incidence exceeds the critical angle, enabling low-loss signal transmission.

concepts.name: Myopia (Short Sight) and Its Correction
concepts.explanation: Eye focuses distant objects in front of the retina; corrected using a diverging (negative power) lens to extend the far point to infinity.

concepts.name: Hyperopia (Long Sight) and Its Correction
concepts.explanation: Eye focuses near objects behind the retina; corrected using a converging (positive power) lens to reduce near point distance.

concepts.name: Condition for Constructive Interference (Light)
concepts.explanation: Bright fringes occur when the path difference between two coherent light waves equals an integer multiple of the wavelength: Δx = mλ (m = 0, 1, 2, ...).

concepts.name: Condition for Destructive Interference (Light)
concepts.explanation: Dark fringes occur when the path difference between two coherent light waves equals a half-integer multiple of the wavelength: Δx = (m + 1/2)λ.

concepts.name: Fringe Spacing in Double-Slit Interference
concepts.explanation: The separation between adjacent bright (or dark) fringes on the screen is β = λL/d, where L is slit-to-screen distance and d is slit separation.

concepts.name: Coherent Light Sources
concepts.explanation: Sources that maintain a constant phase difference and have the same frequency, required to produce stable interference fringes.

concepts.name: Path Difference and Phase Difference (Light Waves)
concepts.explanation: The phase difference between two light waves is related to their path difference by Δϕ = 2πΔx/λ, determining interference outcomes.

concepts.name: Principle of Superposition (Light Waves)
concepts.explanation: The resultant displacement (or intensity) at a point is the sum of contributions from individual waves, underpinning interference patterns.

concepts.name: Single-Slit Diffraction Minima
concepts.explanation: Dark minima in single-slit diffraction occur at angles satisfying a sinθ = mλ (m = 1, 2, ...), where a is the slit width.

concepts.name: Diffraction Grating Equation
concepts.explanation: For a grating of spacing d, principal maxima occur at angles satisfying d sinθ = mλ, producing multiple sharp spectra.

concepts.name: Light as a Transverse Wave
concepts.explanation: Light exhibits transverse wave motion with oscillations perpendicular to the direction of propagation; evidenced by polarization.

concepts.name: Thin-Film Interference
concepts.explanation: Constructive and destructive interference between light reflected from the two surfaces of a thin film produces vivid colors (e.g., petrol films, soap bubbles).

concepts.name: Polarization by Dichroism (Polaroid)
concepts.explanation: Selective absorption of one polarization component by dichroic materials; used in Polaroid sunglasses to reduce glare.

concepts.name: Stress-Induced Birefringence (Photoelasticity)
concepts.explanation: Mechanical stress causes temporary double refraction in transparent materials, producing colored patterns between crossed polarizers.

concepts.name: Diffraction from a Grating (Compact Discs)
concepts.explanation: Regular CD track spacing acts as a diffraction grating, producing iridescent colors governed by the grating equation mλ = d sinθ.

concepts.name: Operation of a Spectrometer
concepts.explanation: Procedure for aligning and using a spectrometer to measure angles, refractive index of a prism, and wavelengths (collimation, focusing, calibration).

concepts.name: Colour and Wavelength
concepts.explanation: Perceived colour relates to the wavelength/frequency composition of light; distinguishes spectral colours from structural colours.

concepts.name: Dispersion in Gemstones (Fire)
concepts.explanation: High dispersion and total internal reflection in cut gemstones separate colors, producing 'fire' and brilliance.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet Absorption by the Ozone Layer
concepts.explanation: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs high-energy UV-B and UV-C radiation, reducing biologically harmful ultraviolet reaching Earth's surface.

concepts.name: Infrared Thermography (Infrared Camera)
concepts.explanation: Imaging technique that detects thermal infrared radiation to map surface temperature distributions; used in medical diagnostics for inflammation and vascular assessment.

concepts.name: Night Vision Using Infrared Imaging
concepts.explanation: Low-light imaging employing IR-sensitive detectors and/or active IR illumination to visualize scenes in darkness; includes thermal imaging and near-IR night vision approaches.

concepts.name: Derivation of the diffraction grating equation
concepts.explanation: Derive the condition for constructive interference from path differences between adjacent slits to obtain nλ = d sinθ.

concepts.name: Polarization of light using Polaroids
concepts.explanation: Demonstrate and explain polarization of transverse light waves and the effect of analyzer orientation on transmitted intensity.

concepts.name: Dispersion of light by a prism
concepts.explanation: Explain separation of white light into its component colors due to wavelength-dependent refractive index in a prism.

concepts.name: Dispersion of light by a diffraction grating
concepts.explanation: Use a grating to separate wavelengths via interference, producing spectra with high angular dispersion and resolution.

concepts.name: Recombination of spectral colors using a prism
concepts.explanation: Demonstrate recombining a dispersed spectrum to form white light using an inverted or second prism.

concepts.name: Primary, secondary, and complementary colors of light
concepts.explanation: Identify RGB as additive primaries, CMY as secondary colors, and complementary color pairs that combine to white.

concepts.name: Detection methods for ultraviolet and infrared radiation
concepts.explanation: Describe methods for detecting UV (e.g., fluorescence, photodiodes) and IR (e.g., thermopiles, bolometers, IR sensors).

concepts.name: Spectrometer: parts and functions
concepts.explanation: Identify and explain the roles of the collimator, prism/grating table, and telescope in spectral measurements.

concepts.name: Verification of Snell's Law of Refraction
concepts.explanation: Experimental confirmation that the ratio of the sines of the angles of incidence and refraction is constant for a given pair of media, i.e., n1 sin i = n2 sin r, typically by plotting sin i versus sin r.

concepts.name: Measurement of Refractive Index of a Liquid or Solid
concepts.explanation: Determine a material’s refractive index using methods such as Snell’s law with a ray box and protractor, apparent depth, critical angle, or a refractometer.

concepts.name: Multiplication as Equal Groups
concepts.explanation: Interprets multiplication as repeated addition and as equal-size groups or arrays.

concepts.name: Ratio and Unit Rate
concepts.explanation: Compares two quantities with ratios and finds the unit rate to model proportional relationships.

concepts.name: Integer Operations with Opposites
concepts.explanation: Adds, subtracts, multiplies, and divides integers using number line models and properties of opposites.

concepts.name: Solving One-Step Linear Equations
concepts.explanation: Uses inverse operations to isolate the variable and maintain equality in linear equations.

concepts.name: Area of Composite Figures
concepts.explanation: Decomposes complex shapes into simpler ones to calculate total area.

concepts.name: Normal Distribution and Z-Score
concepts.explanation: Models data with the normal curve and standardizes values using z-scores for comparison and probability.

concepts.name: Coulomb's Law (Force Between Charges)
concepts.explanation: Quantifies the electrostatic force between point charges: F = k q1 q2 / r^2 along the line joining them, with direction given by like charges repelling and unlike attracting.

concepts.name: Electric Potential Difference
concepts.explanation: Work done per unit charge moving between two points in an electric field, V = W/q; relates to uniform fields by V = Ed over distance d.

concepts.name: Electrification by Induction
concepts.explanation: Charging a conductor without contact by polarizing charges with a nearby charged body and using grounding to separate charges.

concepts.name: Electrification by Contact
concepts.explanation: Charging an object by direct touching or rubbing, transferring charge until electrostatic equilibrium; conserves total charge.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Hazards in Flour Mills
concepts.explanation: Static charge accumulation can ignite dust-air mixtures; safety measures include bonding, grounding, humidity control, and dust management.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Hazards During Aircraft Refueling
concepts.explanation: Fuel flow generates static that can spark; mitigated by bonding the aircraft and fuel truck, grounding, and controlling flow rate.

concepts.name: Dust Attraction on Television Screens
concepts.explanation: Charged screens (especially CRTs) attract dust via electrostatic forces; reduced by antistatic coatings or humidifying the air.

concepts.name: Static Cling on Clothes
concepts.explanation: Triboelectric charging during drying causes garments to adhere; mitigated by fabric softeners, dryer sheets, or increased humidity.

concepts.name: Lightning Conductor (Lightning Rod)
concepts.explanation: A metal rod bonded to earth that provides a low-resistance path for lightning current, protecting structures by safely conducting charge to ground.

concepts.name: Coulomb’s Law
concepts.explanation: The electrostatic force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the separation: F = (1/4πε)·(Q1Q2/r^2).

concepts.name: Electric Field Strength
concepts.explanation: Electric field at a point defined as force per unit positive test charge, E = F/q.

concepts.name: Zero Potential (Reference Potential)
concepts.explanation: Choice of a reference point where electric potential is defined to be zero, often at infinity or ground.

concepts.name: Vector Nature of the Electric Field
concepts.explanation: Electric field has magnitude and direction; fields superpose vectorially.

concepts.name: Superposition of Electrostatic Forces (Collinear Charges)
concepts.explanation: Net force on a charge due to multiple charges on a line is the algebraic sum of individual Coulomb forces.

concepts.name: Conductors and Insulators
concepts.explanation: Materials classified by their ability to allow charge movement; conductors permit free charge motion, insulators do not.

concepts.name: Point Discharge (Corona Discharge)
concepts.explanation: Ionization of air near sharp, highly charged points causing a gradual loss of charge to the surroundings.

concepts.name: Electric Field Mapping with Oil and Semolina
concepts.explanation: Experimental method to visualize 2D electric field patterns using a dielectric and marker particles.

concepts.name: Van de Graaff Generator (Electrostatic Generator)
concepts.explanation: Device that transports charge to a high-potential dome using a moving belt, demonstrating high-voltage electrostatics.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) Hazards to Integrated Circuits
concepts.explanation: Sudden transfer of static charge can damage semiconductor devices; requires handling precautions.

concepts.name: Lightning Conductors (Lightning Rods)
concepts.explanation: Conductive rods provide a low-resistance path to ground, reducing lightning damage by controlling discharge.

concepts.name: Xerography (Electrophotography) Principle
concepts.explanation: Imaging process using photoconductors and electrostatic charges to attract toner and form copies.

concepts.name: Common Uses of Capacitors
concepts.explanation: Applications include tuning circuits, camera flash energy storage, smoothing rectified DC, and filtering signals.

concepts.name: Sources of Electromotive Force (emf)
concepts.explanation: Devices and systems that provide energy per unit charge, e.g., mains supply, chemical cells, lead-acid batteries, dry cells, thermocouples.

concepts.name: Conduction in Materials
concepts.explanation: Mechanisms of charge transport in conductors, insulators, and other materials under an electric field.

concepts.name: Capacitance (C = Q/V)
concepts.explanation: Capacitance is the ratio of charge stored on a conductor to the potential difference across it; C = Q/V, measured in farads (F).

concepts.name: Capacitance of a Parallel-Plate Capacitor (C = ε0εrA/d)
concepts.explanation: For two parallel plates, capacitance increases with plate area and dielectric constant and decreases with plate separation: C = ε0εrA/d.

concepts.name: Energy Stored in a Capacitor (W = 1/2 CV^2)
concepts.explanation: The energy stored in an electrostatic field of a charged capacitor is W = 1/2 CV^2.

concepts.name: Charging and Discharging of a Capacitor
concepts.explanation: When connected in a circuit, capacitor voltage and current change in time during charge/discharge, demonstrable with a lamp or low-voltage DC motor.

concepts.name: Capacitors Conduct AC but Block DC
concepts.explanation: A capacitor allows time-varying currents (AC) due to changing electric fields but blocks steady-state DC once charged.

concepts.name: Interpretation of I–V Graphs
concepts.explanation: Analyzing current–voltage characteristics to determine resistance, identify ohmic and non-ohmic behavior, and extract device parameters.

concepts.name: Electric Current as Rate of Flow of Charge
concepts.explanation: Current is the rate at which charge flows: I = dQ/dt, with 1 A = 1 C s⁻¹.

concepts.name: Potential Difference, Voltage, and EMF
concepts.explanation: Potential difference (voltage) is energy per unit charge between two points; EMF is the source voltage applied to a circuit.

concepts.name: Charge Carriers
concepts.explanation: Particles that carry electric charge in different media: electrons in metals and vacuum, ions in electrolytes and gases, electrons and holes in semiconductors.

concepts.name: Electrical Conduction in Metals
concepts.explanation: Conduction via mobile electrons in a lattice, characterized by electron drift under an electric field.

concepts.name: Electrical Conduction in Ionic Solutions
concepts.explanation: Conduction occurs through movement of positive and negative ions; electrode activity depends on whether electrodes are active or inert.

concepts.name: Electrical Conduction in Gases
concepts.explanation: At sufficient electric fields or ionization, gases conduct via ions and electrons formed by collisions or external ionization sources.

concepts.name: Electrical Conduction in Vacuum
concepts.explanation: Conduction via electron emission (thermionic or field emission) and their motion through vacuum under applied potentials.

concepts.name: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Semiconductor Conduction
concepts.explanation: Intrinsic semiconductors conduct via thermally generated carriers; extrinsic conduction arises from doping that introduces donors or acceptors.

concepts.name: p-type and n-type Semiconductors
concepts.explanation: p-type materials have hole majority carriers (acceptor doping); n-type materials have electron majority carriers (donor doping).

concepts.name: Rectification of AC
concepts.explanation: Conversion of AC to DC using diodes (half-wave or full-wave rectifiers), producing a unidirectional output.

concepts.name: Light-Emitting Diode (LED)
concepts.explanation: A forward-biased p–n junction that emits photons via electron–hole recombination; exhibits a nonlinear I–V characteristic and threshold voltage.

concepts.name: Wheatstone Bridge
concepts.explanation: A four-arm bridge circuit used to determine an unknown resistance by balancing two resistor ratios so that no current flows through the galvanometer.

concepts.name: Balance Condition of a Wheatstone Bridge
concepts.explanation: At balance, the ratio of resistances in one pair of adjacent arms equals that in the other pair (R1/R2 = R3/Rx), giving zero galvanometer current.

concepts.name: Measurement of Unknown Resistance using a Wheatstone Bridge
concepts.explanation: Procedure to adjust known resistors to achieve balance and compute the unknown resistance from Rx = (R2/R1) R3.

concepts.name: Advantage of Using High Voltage (EHT) in Power Transmission
concepts.explanation: Transmitting electrical power at extra-high voltage reduces current for a given power, minimizing I^2R losses and improving efficiency over long distances.

concepts.name: Thermostat as a Temperature Control and Fail-Safe Device
concepts.explanation: A temperature-sensitive switch (e.g., bimetallic or thermistor-based) that regulates heating/cooling and can cut off power to prevent overheating.

concepts.name: Applications of the Chemical Effect of Electric Current
concepts.explanation: Practical uses of electrolysis such as electroplating, electrorefining, anodizing, and electrolytic production of substances.

concepts.name: Resistance Dependence on Length and Cross-Sectional Area
concepts.explanation: For a uniform conductor, resistance increases with length and decreases with cross-sectional area (R ∝ L/A).

concepts.name: p-n Junction: Current Flow Mechanism
concepts.explanation: Explains depletion region and carrier movement that determine current across a semiconductor p-n junction.

concepts.name: Diode Forward and Reverse Bias
concepts.explanation: Forward bias significantly increases current through a p-n junction; reverse bias restricts current except for leakage.

concepts.name: Light-Dependent Resistor (LDR) Characteristics
concepts.explanation: An LDR’s resistance decreases with increasing light intensity; used as a light sensor.

concepts.name: Use of an Ohmmeter
concepts.explanation: Procedure for measuring resistance with an ohmmeter, including correct range selection and ensuring circuits are de-energized.

concepts.name: Measurement of Resistance Using a Metre Bridge
concepts.explanation: Determining unknown resistance by null-balance using the Wheatstone bridge principle on a metre bridge.

concepts.name: Electrical Safety in Domestic Circuits
concepts.explanation: Safe practices in household wiring, including earthing, insulation, and protection devices to prevent shock and fire.

concepts.name: Wiring a Plug
concepts.explanation: Correctly connecting live, neutral, and earth wires, fitting the fuse, and securing the cord grip in a mains plug.

concepts.name: Fuse Rating Calculations
concepts.explanation: Selecting an appropriate fuse by calculating circuit current (I = P/V) and applying a safety margin.

concepts.name: Domestic Fuse Box (Consumer Unit)
concepts.explanation: The distribution and protection center in a home, using fuses/MCBs/RCDs to safeguard circuits.

concepts.name: Electricity Meter (Energy Measurement at Home)
concepts.explanation: Device that measures electrical energy consumption in kilowatt-hours for billing and monitoring usage.

concepts.name: Equivalent Resistance in Series
concepts.explanation: In a series circuit the same current flows through each resistor and the total resistance equals the sum of individual resistances: Rs = R1 + R2 + ... .

concepts.name: Equivalent Resistance in Parallel
concepts.explanation: In a parallel circuit each resistor has the same voltage across it and the total resistance satisfies 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... .

concepts.name: Resistivity (ρ) of a Material
concepts.explanation: An intrinsic property of a material relating resistance to geometry via R = ρ L/A; depends on material and temperature; SI unit is ohm-meter (Ω·m).

concepts.name: Temperature Dependence of Resistivity
concepts.explanation: Resistivity changes with temperature; for many metals ρ ≈ ρ0[1 + α(T − T0)] where α is the temperature coefficient; semiconductors typically show decreasing ρ with T.

concepts.name: Balancing Condition of the Wheatstone Bridge
concepts.explanation: At null deflection, the ratio of resistances in one arm equals the ratio in the other (R1/R2 = R3/Rx), resulting in zero current through the galvanometer.

concepts.name: Measuring Unknown Resistance with a Wheatstone Bridge
concepts.explanation: Procedure to adjust a variable arm until galvanometer null is achieved, then compute the unknown resistance from the balanced ratio.

concepts.name: Light Dependent Resistor (LDR)
concepts.explanation: A photoconductive sensor whose resistance decreases with increasing light intensity, used for light sensing and control circuits.

concepts.name: LDR Resistance–Illumination Characteristic
concepts.explanation: The nonlinear relationship between an LDR's resistance and incident light level, often approximated by a power law and used for calibration and sensing thresholds.

concepts.name: Lenz's law
concepts.explanation: The direction of an induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it.

concepts.name: Magnetic flux (Φ = BA)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic flux through a surface equals the product of magnetic flux density and area for perpendicular fields.

concepts.name: Lorentz force on a moving charge (F = qvB)
concepts.explanation: A charge moving through a magnetic field experiences a force proportional to its charge, speed, and magnetic flux density.

concepts.name: Definition of the ampere using forces between currents
concepts.explanation: The ampere is defined via the force per unit length between two long, parallel conductors carrying current.

concepts.name: Magnetic field of a long straight current-carrying wire
concepts.explanation: A current in a long straight wire produces a circular magnetic field whose strength decreases with distance.

concepts.name: Magnetic field of a circular current loop
concepts.explanation: A current loop produces a magnetic field similar to a short bar magnet, with an axial field through the loop's center.

concepts.name: Magnetic field inside a solenoid
concepts.explanation: A current through a solenoid creates a nearly uniform magnetic field inside the coil, with strength depending on turns and current.

concepts.name: Transformer operation and turns ratio
concepts.explanation: Alternating current in a primary coil induces a voltage in a secondary coil; voltages relate to turns ratio for ideal transformers.

concepts.name: Alternating current (AC) basics
concepts.explanation: Electric current that periodically reverses direction, characterized by frequency, amplitude, and rms values.

concepts.name: Electric generator principle
concepts.explanation: Mechanical motion in a magnetic field changes flux through a circuit, inducing an emf and converting mechanical to electrical energy.

concepts.name: Joule heating in conductors (W = I^2 R t)
concepts.explanation: Electrical energy dissipated as heat in a resistor equals current squared times resistance times time.

concepts.name: Kilowatt-hour as a unit of electrical energy
concepts.explanation: The kWh is the energy used by a 1 kW load running for one hour, commonly used for billing.

concepts.name: Fuse operation and rating
concepts.explanation: A sacrificial safety device that melts to interrupt excessive current; correct rating protects circuits and appliances.

concepts.name: Ring vs radial circuit topologies
concepts.explanation: Domestic wiring layouts where outlets are supplied by a loop (ring) or single run (radial), affecting protection and load distribution.

concepts.name: Electromagnets
concepts.explanation: Magnetic fields produced by current-carrying coils; strength depends on current, turns, and core material; used in relays, motors, and lifting.

concepts.name: Magnetic poles exist in pairs
concepts.explanation: Isolated magnetic poles are not observed; magnets have inseparable north and south poles.

concepts.name: Earth’s magnetic field and navigation
concepts.explanation: The Earth acts like a giant magnet, enabling compass-based navigation using the direction of its magnetic field.

concepts.name: AC power transmission and the national grid
concepts.explanation: Use of alternating current and transformers to transmit electrical power efficiently over long distances.

concepts.name: Alternating Voltage and Current as Functions of Time
concepts.explanation: In AC circuits, voltage and current vary periodically with time (often sinusoidally) and are characterized by amplitude, frequency, and period.

concepts.name: RMS Value of an AC Signal
concepts.explanation: Defines the root-mean-square value as the DC-equivalent for power; for a sinusoid Vrms = Vpeak/√2 and Irms = Ipeak/√2; used to compare with peak values.

concepts.name: Conversion Between Peak, Peak-to-Peak, and RMS Voltages
concepts.explanation: Carry out calculations converting between Vpeak, Vpp, and Vrms for sinusoidal AC to support specification and measurement.

concepts.name: Using an Oscilloscope to Display and Measure AC Waveforms
concepts.explanation: Set timebase and voltage scales to display AC waveforms; measure period, frequency, and peak-to-peak voltage from the screen.

concepts.name: Transformer Structure and Principle of Operation
concepts.explanation: A transformer has primary and secondary windings on a magnetic core; AC in the primary produces changing flux that induces emf in the secondary proportional to the turns ratio.

concepts.name: Qualitative Effects of Inductors in AC Circuits
concepts.explanation: Inductors oppose changes in current and limit AC current flow more at higher frequencies; qualitative understanding without mathematical phase analysis.

concepts.name: Inductor as Ballast in Lighting Circuits
concepts.explanation: Use of a series inductor to limit current in discharge lamps (e.g., fluorescent lighting) to ensure stable operation.

concepts.name: Joule’s Law of Heating: Experimental Verification (Δθ ∝ I^2)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory verification that the temperature rise of a resistor (or calorimeter content) is proportional to the square of the current for fixed resistance and time, consistent with H = I^2 R t.

concepts.name: Measurement of Electrical Resistivity of a Wire
concepts.explanation: Determine a wire’s resistivity using ρ = R A / L by measuring its resistance, length, and cross-sectional area (via micrometer/vernier), typically employing a bridge or ohmmeter.

concepts.name: Temperature Dependence of Resistance in Metallic Conductors
concepts.explanation: Investigate how a metal’s resistance varies with temperature and estimate the temperature coefficient of resistance by measuring R versus T.

concepts.name: Investigation of thermistor resistance versus temperature
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to measure how a thermistor's resistance changes with temperature by varying temperature in controlled steps, measuring resistance (or V and I), and plotting an R-T curve to interpret behavior.

concepts.name: Negative temperature coefficient (NTC) behavior of thermistors
concepts.explanation: In an NTC thermistor the resistance decreases as temperature increases, often modeled by R = R0 exp[B(1/T − 1/T0)], enabling temperature sensing via resistance measurement.

concepts.name: Current–Voltage (I–V) Characteristics
concepts.explanation: The relationship between current through and potential difference across a component, obtained by measuring and plotting I against V to reveal linear (ohmic) or nonlinear behavior.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristic of a Metallic Conductor (Ohmic Behavior)
concepts.explanation: At constant temperature, current is directly proportional to potential difference, yielding a straight-line I–V graph with constant resistance in accordance with Ohm's law.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristic of a Filament Bulb (Temperature-Dependent Resistance)
concepts.explanation: A filament lamp shows non-ohmic behavior; as current increases the filament heats up, raising its resistance and producing a curved I–V graph that flattens at higher voltages.

concepts.name: Ionic Conduction in Copper Sulfate Solution: I–V Behavior
