concepts.explanation: An aqueous CuSO4 solution with copper electrodes conducts via ions; measuring I versus V illustrates electrolytic conduction, including effects such as electrode polarization and concentration.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristic of a Semiconductor Diode (Forward and Reverse Bias)
concepts.explanation: A diode exhibits a nonlinear I–V curve with a forward threshold (turn-on) and very small reverse current up to breakdown, demonstrating rectification.

concepts.name: Temperature Dependence of Resistance in Metals
concepts.explanation: In metallic conductors the resistance increases with temperature due to increased lattice vibrations, leading to a positive temperature coefficient as seen in hot filaments.

concepts.name: Experimental Method for Measuring I–V Curves
concepts.explanation: Set up a circuit with an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel, vary the applied voltage, record I and V, control temperature and other variables, and plot I against V for analysis.

concepts.name: X-ray production in X-ray tube
concepts.explanation: Generation of X-rays when high-speed electrons are decelerated in a target, producing bremsstrahlung and characteristic spectra.

concepts.name: Cathode ray oscilloscope (CRO)
concepts.explanation: Instrument that uses an electron beam and deflection plates to display voltage versus time, enabling measurement of amplitude, frequency, and phase.

concepts.name: Cathode ray tube (CRT) operation in television
concepts.explanation: Formation of images by scanning an electron beam across a phosphor screen with controlled deflection and synchronization.

concepts.name: Photoelectric sensors (operation and applications)
concepts.explanation: Devices that convert incident light into electrical signals via photoemission or photoconductivity for control tasks such as burglar alarms and automatic doors.

concepts.name: Displaying ECG/EEG signals on a CRO
concepts.explanation: Using a CRO to visualize biomedical electrical signals by appropriate input coupling, vertical scaling, and time-base settings.

concepts.name: Photoelectric Effect Demonstration with Zinc Plate and Electroscope
concepts.explanation: Shows emission of electrons from a clean zinc plate when illuminated by suitable radiation, detected by discharge of a charged electroscope.

concepts.name: Production of an Electron Beam in a Cathode Ray Tube
concepts.explanation: Generation and focusing of a narrow stream of electrons in a vacuum tube for observation and measurement.

concepts.name: Electron Deflection in Electric Fields
concepts.explanation: Demonstrates how an electron beam is accelerated or deflected by uniform electric fields between charged plates.
concepts.broader_concept: Charged Particle Motion in Electric Fields

concepts.name: Electron Deflection in Magnetic Fields
concepts.explanation: Demonstrates curvature of an electron beam due to the magnetic force perpendicular to its velocity and the field.
concepts.broader_concept: Charged Particle Motion in Magnetic Fields

concepts.name: X-ray Radiation Hazards and Safety
concepts.explanation: Identifies biological risks of ionizing X-ray exposure and outlines shielding, time, and distance controls for protection.

concepts.name: Electron Mass and Atomic Location
concepts.explanation: Understanding the electron’s small mass (~9.11×10^-31 kg) and its location in atomic orbitals around the nucleus as part of atomic structure.

concepts.name: Electronvolt and Energy Scales (eV, keV, MeV, GeV)
concepts.explanation: Definition of 1 eV as the energy gained by an electron accelerated through 1 V (1.602×10^-19 J) and use of multiples keV, MeV, GeV for atomic, nuclear, and particle energies.
concepts.broader_concept: Energy Units in Atomic and Nuclear Physics

concepts.name: Photocell (Photoelectric Cell) Operation
concepts.explanation: Demonstration device for the photoelectric effect where light incident on a photosensitive cathode produces a measurable photocurrent dependent on intensity and frequency.

concepts.name: Thermionic Emission and Electron Beam Production
concepts.explanation: Emission of electrons from a heated metal cathode and their acceleration into a directed beam using electric fields; basis of electron guns.

concepts.name: Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) Structure and Operation
concepts.explanation: Vacuum tube with an electron gun, accelerating/focusing anodes, deflection system, and fluorescent screen used to produce and control electron beams.

concepts.name: Photon as Quantum of Energy
concepts.explanation: Concept that electromagnetic radiation consists of discrete packets (photons), each carrying energy proportional to its frequency.

concepts.name: Planck Relation (E = hf)
concepts.explanation: Formula giving the energy of a photon as the product of Planck’s constant and the light frequency, used in photoelectric and quantum calculations.

concepts.name: Cathode-Ray Tube Components (Filament, Cathode, Anode, Screen)
concepts.explanation: Identification and function of CRT parts: heated filament and cathode as electron source, anode for acceleration/focusing, and fluorescent screen for visualization.

concepts.name: Einstein's Photoelectric Law
concepts.explanation: Relates the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons to photon energy minus the work function: KE_max = hf − φ.

concepts.name: Threshold Frequency
concepts.explanation: The minimum frequency of incident light required to eject electrons from a material's surface in the photoelectric effect.

concepts.name: X-ray Production by Electron Target Collisions
concepts.explanation: Generation of X-rays when high-energy electrons decelerate in a target, producing bremsstrahlung and characteristic radiation.

concepts.name: Hot-Cathode X-ray Tube Principles
concepts.explanation: Electrons thermionically emitted from a heated cathode are accelerated by high voltage to strike an anode target, producing X-rays.

concepts.name: Properties of X-rays
concepts.explanation: X-rays are electromagnetic waves with high penetration and strong ionising ability; they travel at light speed and are neutral.

concepts.name: Bohr Model of the Atom
concepts.explanation: Electrons occupy quantised orbits with discrete energies; transitions between levels emit or absorb photons.

concepts.name: Rutherford Scattering Experiment Principle
concepts.explanation: Alpha particles scattered by thin foil reveal a small, dense, positively charged nucleus at the atom's center.

concepts.name: Structure of the Atom
concepts.explanation: Atoms consist of a central nucleus surrounded by electrons; most atomic volume is empty space.

concepts.name: Atomic Nucleus (Protons and Neutrons)
concepts.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons (nucleons) that account for most atomic mass and define nuclear properties.

concepts.name: Isotopic Notation AZX
concepts.explanation: Representation of nuclides using mass number A, atomic number Z, and element symbol X; identifies isotopes.

concepts.name: Experimental Identification of Alpha, Beta, Gamma
concepts.explanation: Use deflection in electric/magnetic fields and measurements of ionisation/penetration to distinguish radiation types.

concepts.name: Changes in A and Z During Radioactive Decay
concepts.explanation: Rules for how mass number and atomic number change in alpha, beta, and gamma decay processes.

concepts.name: Law of Radioactive Decay
concepts.explanation: The number of undecayed nuclei decreases exponentially with time: N(t) = N0 e^(−λt).

concepts.name: Decay Constant and Activity (rate = λN)
concepts.explanation: Activity is proportional to the number of nuclei present: A = −dN/dt = λN; λ characterises decay probability per unit time.

concepts.name: Half-life and T1/2 = ln 2 / λ
concepts.explanation: Half-life is the time for activity or number of nuclei to halve; T1/2 is related to decay constant by T1/2 = ln2/λ.

concepts.name: Principle of Operation of a G-M Tube or Solid-State Detector
concepts.explanation: Ionising radiation produces charge in a fill gas or semiconductor, creating pulses that are counted as detection events.

concepts.name: Principles of Nuclear Fusion
concepts.explanation: Light nuclei combine to form heavier ones, releasing energy; fusion powers the Sun and stars.

concepts.name: Radiation Protection Principles
concepts.explanation: Minimise dose using time, distance, and shielding; apply procedures to control exposure and waste.

concepts.name: Background Radiation and Radon
concepts.explanation: Natural sources of ionising radiation include cosmic rays, terrestrial sources like granite, and radon gas.

concepts.name: Applications of Radioisotopes
concepts.explanation: Use of radioisotopes in medical imaging and therapy, food irradiation, agriculture, radiocarbon dating, smoke detection, and industry.

concepts.name: Spectroscopy as a Scientific Tool
concepts.explanation: Analysis of line and continuous spectra to infer atomic structure, composition, and physical conditions.

concepts.name: Basic Laser Principle (Stimulated Emission)
concepts.explanation: Coherent light generation via population inversion and stimulated emission in an optical cavity.

concepts.name: X-ray Production as Inverse Photoelectric Effect
concepts.explanation: Conceptual link where energy from accelerated electrons is converted into photons in a target, the reverse of photoelectric absorption.

concepts.name: Health Effects of Ionising Radiation
concepts.explanation: Biological damage caused by ionisation in tissues; severity depends on radiation type, source activity, exposure time, and the tissue irradiated.

concepts.name: Becquerel (Bq) — Unit of Radioactivity
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of activity; 1 Bq equals one nuclear decay per second, quantifying how active a radioactive source is.

concepts.name: Source Activity and Exposure Risk
concepts.explanation: Higher activity means more decays per second, increasing emission rate and potential dose rate to nearby tissue.

concepts.name: Exposure Time and Radiation Dose
concepts.explanation: Radiation dose generally increases with the duration of exposure; limiting time reduces risk.

concepts.name: Tissue Radiosensitivity
concepts.explanation: Different tissues exhibit varying sensitivity to ionising radiation, influencing effective dose and health risk.

concepts.name: Environmental (Background) Radiation
concepts.explanation: Ubiquitous ionising radiation from natural and artificial sources contributes to human exposure independent of medical or industrial use.

concepts.name: Decimal to Fraction Conversion
concepts.explanation: Rewriting decimals as fractions in simplest form and vice versa.

concepts.name: Order of Operations
concepts.explanation: Applying a conventional sequence (PEMDAS) to evaluate expressions.

concepts.name: Linear Equations
concepts.explanation: Solving equations that model straight-line relationships between variables.

concepts.name: Slope-Intercept Form
concepts.explanation: Representing a line as y = mx + b to identify slope and y-intercept.

concepts.name: Area of a Triangle
concepts.explanation: Calculating area using one-half base times height.

concepts.name: Volume of a Rectangular Prism
concepts.explanation: Computing volume as length × width × height for prisms.

concepts.name: Angle Relationships
concepts.explanation: Using complementary, supplementary, vertical, and adjacent angle properties.

concepts.name: Similarity
concepts.explanation: Determining when figures have the same shape with proportional side lengths.

concepts.name: Conservation of Energy and Momentum in Particle Reactions
concepts.explanation: In all nuclear decays and particle collisions, total energy and total momentum are conserved and used to analyze reaction outcomes.

concepts.name: Mass–Energy Equivalence (E=mc^2)
concepts.explanation: Mass can be converted to and from other forms of energy; governs particle creation and reaction energetics.

concepts.name: Quark Model
concepts.explanation: Framework in which hadrons are composed of quarks; six flavors (up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom) organize hadronic matter.
concepts.broader_concept: The Standard Model of Particle Physics

concepts.name: Leptons
concepts.explanation: Elementary particles not subject to the strong interaction; examples include the electron, positron, and neutrino.

concepts.name: Baryons
concepts.explanation: Hadrons composed of three quarks and subject to all fundamental forces; examples are protons and neutrons.

concepts.name: Mesons
concepts.explanation: Hadrons consisting of a quark–antiquark pair; subject to the strong interaction and typically lighter than baryons.

concepts.name: Quark Charges (+2/3 and −1/3)
concepts.explanation: Up-type quarks carry charge +2/3e and down-type quarks carry −1/3e; these fractional charges determine hadron charges.

concepts.name: Quark Composition of Nucleons
concepts.explanation: Proton has quark content uud and neutron has udd; baryons are built from three quarks.

concepts.name: Meson Quark–Antiquark Composition
concepts.explanation: Mesons are formed from a quark and an antiquark; various combinations yield different meson species.

concepts.name: Determining Hadron Charge from Quark Content
concepts.explanation: Calculate a hadron’s net charge by summing the fractional charges of its constituent quarks.

concepts.name: Antimatter and Antiparticles
concepts.explanation: Every particle has a corresponding antiparticle with the same mass and opposite charge; antiquarks have opposite charge to quarks.

concepts.name: Pair Production
concepts.explanation: A high-energy photon can convert into a particle–antiparticle pair (e.g., e+e−) near a nucleus, conserving charge, energy, and momentum.

concepts.name: Electron–Positron Annihilation
concepts.explanation: An electron and positron annihilate to produce two gamma photons, conserving energy and momentum.

concepts.name: Neutrino Inference from Beta Decay
concepts.explanation: Missing energy and momentum in beta decay imply emission of a neutrino in addition to the observed particles.

concepts.name: Strong Nuclear Force
concepts.explanation: Short-range force that binds nucleons and acts on quarks and gluons; dominates at femtometer scales.

concepts.name: Weak Nuclear Force
concepts.explanation: Short-range interaction responsible for processes like beta decay; acts on quarks and leptons.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic Force (Inverse-Square)
concepts.explanation: Force between charged particles obeying an inverse-square law; mediates many particle interactions.

concepts.name: Gravitational Force (Inverse-Square)
concepts.explanation: Attractive inverse-square force between masses; negligible in most particle-scale processes.

concepts.name: Particle Accelerators
concepts.explanation: Devices (e.g., circular accelerators) that accelerate charged particles to high energies for collision and discovery of new particles.

concepts.name: Proton–Proton Collisions and Particle Production
concepts.explanation: High-energy pp collisions can convert kinetic energy into new particle–antiparticle pairs.

concepts.name: Cockcroft–Walton Experiment
concepts.explanation: First artificial nuclear disintegration: 1 MeV protons on lithium produced two alpha particles, confirming mass–energy conversion.

concepts.name: Q-value of a Nuclear Reaction
concepts.explanation: Net energy released or absorbed in a reaction, computed from mass differences; positive Q indicates energy release.

concepts.name: Area of Rectangles
concepts.explanation: Area is found by multiplying side lengths (A = l × w) and counting unit squares.

concepts.name: Commutative Property of Multiplication
concepts.explanation: Changing the order of factors does not change the product (ab = ba).

concepts.name: Similar Triangles
concepts.explanation: Triangles with equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding side lengths.

concepts.name: Exponential Growth
concepts.explanation: Growth by a constant percentage per interval; modeled by y = a·b^x with b > 1.

concepts.name: Derivative as Rate of Change
concepts.explanation: The derivative gives the instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line at a point.

concepts.name: Percent Increase and Decrease
concepts.explanation: Use ratios to calculate percent change and solve markdown, markup, and tax problems.

concepts.name: Quadratic Functions and Their Graphs
concepts.explanation: Analyze parabolas in vertex and standard form, including zeros, vertex, and axis of symmetry.

concepts.name: Descriptive Statistics: Mean, Median, Mode
concepts.explanation: Summarize data using measures of central tendency and describe variability.

concepts.name: Compound Probability and Counting Principles
concepts.explanation: Compute probabilities using multiplication/addition rules and count outcomes with permutations and combinations.

concepts.name: Definite Integral as Accumulation
concepts.explanation: Interpret integrals as signed area and accumulation, linked to antiderivatives by the Fundamental Theorem.

concepts.name: Matrix Multiplication and Linear Transformations
concepts.explanation: Use matrices to represent and compose linear transformations and solve systems.

concepts.name: Unit Rate
concepts.explanation: Determining the rate for one unit to compare ratios and solve proportional problems.

concepts.name: Solving Quadratic Equations by Factoring
concepts.explanation: Rewriting a quadratic as a product of binomials and using the zero-product property to find solutions.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic induction
concepts.explanation: A changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces an emf; magnitude given by Faraday’s law and direction by Lenz’s law.

concepts.name: Alternating current (AC)
concepts.explanation: Electric current that reverses direction periodically; characterized by frequency, period, and RMS quantities.

concepts.name: Structure and operation of a simple AC generator
concepts.explanation: A rotating coil in a magnetic field produces an alternating emf via electromagnetic induction; includes slip rings and brushes.

concepts.name: Full-wave rectification using a bridge rectifier with smoothing capacitor
concepts.explanation: A four-diode bridge converts both halves of AC to pulsating DC; a capacitor filter reduces ripple to obtain smoother DC.

concepts.name: Half-wave rectification with a p–n diode
concepts.explanation: A single diode passes only one half-cycle of AC to produce a pulsating DC output.

concepts.name: Factors affecting efficiency of transformers
concepts.explanation: Efficiency depends on copper losses, core losses (hysteresis and eddy currents), leakage flux, and load conditions.

concepts.name: Principle of induction motor
concepts.explanation: A rotating magnetic field induces currents in the rotor, producing torque and continuous rotation.

concepts.name: Simple DC motor
concepts.explanation: A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences torque; a commutator reverses current each half-turn to sustain rotation.

concepts.name: Principle of moving-coil galvanometer
concepts.explanation: A coil in a radial magnetic field experiences a torque proportional to current, producing a measurable deflection.

concepts.name: Conversion of a galvanometer to an ammeter
concepts.explanation: Adding a shunt resistor in parallel with the galvanometer extends its current range; shunt value is calculated from full-scale current and internal resistance.

concepts.name: Conversion of a galvanometer to a voltmeter
concepts.explanation: Adding a multiplier resistor in series with the galvanometer allows measurement of larger voltages; resistor chosen from desired range and meter sensitivity.

concepts.name: Conversion of a galvanometer to an ohmmeter
concepts.explanation: Using a galvanometer with a battery and resistors to measure resistance by current deflection; includes zero-adjust calibration.

concepts.name: Ammeter and voltmeter calculations
concepts.explanation: Calculate expected meter readings and effects of internal resistance when meters are placed in circuits (excluding ohmmeter analyses).

concepts.name: Magnetic field of a solenoid carrying current
concepts.explanation: A current through a solenoid produces a near-uniform internal magnetic field proportional to turn density and current; behaves like a bar magnet.

concepts.name: Transistor as a switch
concepts.explanation: Using a BJT in cutoff and saturation to control loads (e.g., driving a relay) from a small input current.

concepts.name: Transistor implementation of NOT gate (inverter)
concepts.explanation: A single-transistor circuit that inverts the input logic level, realizing a NOT operation.

concepts.name: Truth tables for AND, OR, and NOT gates
concepts.explanation: Constructing tables that list outputs for all possible input combinations for basic logic gates.

concepts.name: Using integrated circuits to implement logic gates in simple circuits
concepts.explanation: Employing IC gate packages to build and test digital circuits that demonstrate AND, OR, and NOT operations.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic relay
concepts.explanation: A coil-operated switch that uses a magnetic field to open or close contacts, enabling low-power control of higher-power circuits.

concepts.name: Moving-coil loudspeaker: principle of operation
concepts.explanation: An alternating current in the voice coil produces a force in a magnetic field, driving a diaphragm to generate sound.

concepts.name: Induction coil (ignition coil) operation
concepts.explanation: A transformer with an interrupter that uses mutual induction to generate high-voltage pulses from a DC source.

concepts.name: LED operation and optical display applications
concepts.explanation: A forward-biased p–n junction emits light via electron–hole recombination; used as indicators and in display arrays.

concepts.name: Fiber optic receiver using photodiode
concepts.explanation: A photodiode converts modulated light in an optical fiber into electrical signals, often followed by amplification and signal conditioning.

concepts.name: Light-emitting diode (LED): principle of operation
concepts.explanation: A forward-biased p–n junction where electron–hole recombination across the band gap releases energy as photons (electroluminescence); the emission wavelength is set by the semiconductor band gap.

concepts.name: Photodiode: principle of operation
concepts.explanation: A p–n junction operated typically under reverse bias where incident photons create electron–hole pairs, producing a photocurrent approximately proportional to light intensity.

concepts.name: Basic structure of a bipolar junction transistor (BJT)
concepts.explanation: A three-layer semiconductor device (npn or pnp) comprising emitter, base, and collector regions with two p–n junctions and differing doping levels, enabling carrier injection and control for amplification/switching.

concepts.name: Electroluminescence in Semiconductors
concepts.explanation: Light emission from a semiconductor caused by carrier injection and radiative recombination across the band gap under forward bias; the physical basis of LED operation.

concepts.name: Photon Energy–Band Gap Relation in LEDs
concepts.explanation: The emitted photon energy approximately equals the semiconductor band gap: E ≈ Eg = hf = hc/λ, which sets the LED’s color and wavelength.

concepts.name: Forward Biasing and Current Limiting for LEDs
concepts.explanation: Procedure to operate an LED safely by applying correct polarity and using a series resistor to set current: R = (Vsupply − Vf)/I.

concepts.name: LED I–V Characteristic and Threshold Voltage
concepts.explanation: LEDs exhibit an exponential I–V relation with a material-dependent forward (knee) voltage; beyond threshold, small voltage changes cause large current changes.

concepts.name: Electron
concepts.explanation: A negatively charged lepton (e−) that orbits the atomic nucleus; fundamental particle with charge −e and very small mass.

concepts.name: Proton
concepts.explanation: A positively charged baryon (p) in the atomic nucleus; composed of two up quarks and one down quark (uud), charge +e.

concepts.name: Neutron
concepts.explanation: An electrically neutral baryon (n) in the atomic nucleus; composed of one up quark and two down quarks (udd).

concepts.name: Nucleons (Protons and Neutrons)
concepts.explanation: Collective term for the particles that make up the atomic nucleus: protons and neutrons.

concepts.name: Positron (Antielectron)
concepts.explanation: The antiparticle of the electron (e+); same mass as the electron but charge +e; annihilates with electrons to produce photons.

concepts.name: Neutrino
concepts.explanation: A neutral lepton (ν) with very small mass that interacts via the weak force; produced in beta decay and other nuclear processes.

concepts.name: Quark Flavors (u, d, s, c, t, b)
concepts.explanation: The six types of quarks—up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom—with fractional electric charges; combine to form hadrons.

concepts.name: Antiquarks
concepts.explanation: Antiparticles of quarks with opposite quantum numbers (e.g., ū, d̄); combine with quarks to form mesons and with antiquarks to form antibaryons.

concepts.name: Force
concepts.explanation: An interaction that changes an object's motion; the net force causes acceleration according to F = m a.

concepts.name: Work
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred when a force causes displacement: W = F s cos(θ).

concepts.name: Potential Energy
concepts.explanation: Stored energy due to position or configuration; for gravity near Earth Ep = m g h.

concepts.name: Momentum
concepts.explanation: Product of mass and velocity, p = m v; conserved in isolated systems.

concepts.name: Acceleration
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of velocity, a = dv/dt; central to kinematics and Newton's laws.

concepts.name: Velocity
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of displacement (vector); instantaneous velocity v = ds/dt.

concepts.name: Speed
concepts.explanation: Scalar rate of motion; average speed = total distance / time.

concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.explanation: Vector from initial to final position; can be positive or negative along a line.

concepts.name: Distance
concepts.explanation: Scalar path length traveled irrespective of direction.

concepts.name: Acceleration due to Gravity
concepts.explanation: Free-fall acceleration near Earth's surface, g ≈ 9.8 m s^-2; assumed constant near the surface.

concepts.name: Gravitational Field Strength
concepts.explanation: Force per unit mass at a point in a gravitational field: g = F/m (N kg^-1).

concepts.name: Weight
concepts.explanation: Gravitational force acting on a mass: W = m g; varies with local g.

concepts.name: Gravitational Constant (G)
concepts.explanation: Universal constant in Newton's law of gravitation that sets the strength of gravitational attraction.

concepts.name: Torque (Moment of a Couple)
concepts.explanation: Turning effect produced by a pair of equal and opposite forces separated by a distance: τ = F d.

concepts.name: Moment of a Force
concepts.explanation: Turning effect of a single force about a pivot: M = F r⊥; used in equilibrium conditions.

concepts.name: Angular Velocity
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of angular displacement: ω = dθ/dt; relates to linear speed by v = r ω.

concepts.name: Pressure
concepts.explanation: Force per unit area: P = F/A; in fluids increases with depth by P = ρ g h.

concepts.name: Density
concepts.explanation: Mass per unit volume: ρ = m/V; key to buoyancy and material identification.

concepts.name: Period (Periodic Time)
concepts.explanation: Time for one complete cycle of a repeating motion: T = 1/f.

concepts.name: Temperature (Kelvin Scale)
concepts.explanation: Thermodynamic temperature measured in kelvins with absolute zero as the zero point.

concepts.name: Electronvolt (eV)
concepts.explanation: Energy gained by a charge of one electron moved through 1 volt; 1 eV = 1.602 × 10^-19 J.

concepts.name: Kilowatt-hour (kWh)
concepts.explanation: Practical electrical energy unit equal to 3.6 × 10^6 J; used in energy billing.

concepts.name: Radian Measure of Angle
concepts.explanation: Angular measure based on arc length; fundamental for angular kinematics (2π rad = 360°).

concepts.name: Mass
concepts.explanation: Measure of inertia and amount of matter; relates force and acceleration via F = m a.

concepts.name: Symbol T for thermodynamic temperature (kelvin, K)
concepts.explanation: Standard symbol T denotes absolute thermodynamic temperature measured in kelvin (SI base unit K).

concepts.name: Symbol t for temperature in degrees Celsius (°C)
concepts.explanation: Conventional symbol t represents temperature values expressed on the Celsius scale, in degrees Celsius (°C).

concepts.name: Symbol θ for temperature in degrees Celsius (°C)
concepts.explanation: Symbol θ is used in some contexts (e.g., thermal physics) to represent temperature on the Celsius scale, in degrees Celsius (°C).

concepts.name: Temperature Change (Δθ)
concepts.explanation: The difference between final and initial temperatures of a system, commonly used as Δθ in thermal energy calculations such as Q = mcΔθ.

concepts.name: Degree Celsius (°C)
concepts.explanation: A unit for measuring temperature on the Celsius scale, where equal increments correspond to equal thermal intervals.

concepts.name: Heat (Q)
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred between bodies due to a temperature difference; denoted by Q and measured in joules (J).

concepts.name: Joule (J) as SI Unit of Heat and Energy
concepts.explanation: The joule (J) is the SI unit for energy, including heat Q; it quantifies thermal energy in calculations and experiments.

concepts.name: Heat Capacity (C)
concepts.explanation: The amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a body by 1 K; an extensive property with SI unit J K^-1. Related by C = m c and Q = C ΔT.

concepts.name: Unit of Specific Heat Capacity (J kg^-1 K^-1)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit for specific heat capacity, indicating energy per kilogram per kelvin.

concepts.name: Unit of Heat Capacity (J K^-1)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit for heat capacity, indicating energy required per kelvin temperature change for a body.

concepts.name: Specific Heat Capacity (c)
concepts.explanation: Amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K; symbol c; SI unit J kg^-1 K^-1.

concepts.name: Units of Specific Heat Capacity
concepts.explanation: Understanding and converting units for specific heat capacity, primarily J kg^-1 K^-1 and kJ kg^-1 K^-1.

concepts.name: Specific Latent Heat (L)
concepts.explanation: Energy required per kilogram to change a substance's phase at constant temperature; SI unit J kg^-1.

concepts.name: Heat During Phase Change: Q = mL
concepts.explanation: Calculates the heat absorbed or released during a phase change using mass and specific latent heat.

concepts.name: Joule (J) — SI Unit of Energy
concepts.explanation: Standard SI unit for energy, work, and heat; used to express heat and latent heat quantities.

concepts.name: Wave Speed (v = fλ)
concepts.explanation: The speed at which a wave propagates, equal to the product of its frequency and wavelength.

concepts.name: Frequency of a Wave
concepts.explanation: Number of oscillations per second of a periodic wave, measured in hertz (Hz).

concepts.name: Amplitude of a Wave
concepts.explanation: Maximum displacement from equilibrium of a wave, indicating its energy, measured in metres (m).

concepts.name: Snell's Law (Refraction)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between angles and refractive indices at an interface: n1 sin i = n2 sin r.

concepts.name: Law of Reflection
concepts.explanation: At a reflective surface, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, measured from the normal.

concepts.name: Critical Angle and Total Internal Reflection
concepts.explanation: For light in a denser-to-rarer medium, the critical angle yields a refracted angle of 90°; larger incidence causes total internal reflection.

concepts.name: Lens Formula (1/f = 1/u + 1/v)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between focal length f, object distance u, and image distance v for thin lenses.

concepts.name: Magnification (Lenses and Mirrors)
concepts.explanation: Ratio of image size to object size; for thin lenses m = v/u (dimensionless).

concepts.name: Power of a Lens (Dioptre)
concepts.explanation: Measure of a lens's converging or diverging ability, P = 1/f with f in metres (unit: m⁻¹).

concepts.name: Wave Speed on a Stretched String
concepts.explanation: Speed of transverse waves on a string depends on tension T and linear mass density μ: v = √(T/μ).

concepts.name: Sound Intensity Level (Decibel)
concepts.explanation: Logarithmic measure of sound intensity relative to a reference: L = 10 log10(I/I0), unit dB.

concepts.name: Young’s Double-Slit Interference
concepts.explanation: Interference fringe spacing on a screen given by w = λL/d, where d is slit separation.

concepts.name: Speed of Electromagnetic Waves in Vacuum
concepts.explanation: Electromagnetic waves propagate in vacuum at c ≈ 3.0 × 10^8 m s⁻¹.

concepts.name: Atomic Number (Z)
concepts.explanation: The number of protons in an atom’s nucleus; defines the element and its position in the periodic table.

concepts.name: Mass Number (A)
concepts.explanation: The total number of protons and neutrons (nucleons) in the nucleus; distinguishes isotopes of an element.

concepts.name: Half-life (T1/2)
concepts.explanation: The time taken for the number of undecayed nuclei or the activity of a radioactive sample to fall to half its initial value.

concepts.name: Radioactive Decay Constant (λ)
concepts.explanation: The probability per unit time that a nucleus decays; relates to half-life by T1/2 = ln(2)/λ and to activity via A = λN.

concepts.name: Activity of a Radioactive Source (A)
concepts.explanation: The rate of nuclear decays in a sample, measured in becquerels (decays per second); given by A = λN.

concepts.name: Planck Constant (h)
concepts.explanation: Fundamental constant linking photon energy to frequency via E = hf; central to quantum theory.

concepts.name: Electronic Charge (e)
concepts.explanation: The magnitude of the charge on an electron; the fundamental unit of charge such that Q = ne for integer n.

concepts.name: Diode Rectifier
concepts.explanation: Use of a p–n junction diode to convert AC to DC (half-wave/full-wave), including ripple and smoothing with capacitors.

concepts.name: NPN Junction Transistor
concepts.explanation: A bipolar junction transistor where electrons are the majority carriers; operation in cutoff, active, and saturation regions for switching and amplification.

concepts.name: PNP Junction Transistor
concepts.explanation: A bipolar junction transistor with holes as majority carriers; biasing and operation modes analogous to NPN but with reversed polarities.

concepts.name: Photovoltaic Cell
concepts.explanation: A semiconductor device that converts light into electrical energy via the photovoltaic effect; I–V characteristics and power output depend on irradiance and temperature.

concepts.name: DC Motor
concepts.explanation: An electric machine that converts electrical energy to mechanical rotation using the motor effect (force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field).

concepts.name: Electromagnetic Loudspeaker
concepts.explanation: An electroacoustic transducer where a voice coil in a magnetic field converts electrical signals into sound via diaphragm motion.

concepts.name: Dynamic Microphone
concepts.explanation: A microphone that uses electromagnetic induction: diaphragm motion moves a coil in a magnetic field to generate a voltage proportional to sound pressure.

concepts.name: Electric Bell
concepts.explanation: An electromagnet-driven make-and-break device producing sound through repeated armature strikes when current flows.

concepts.name: Earphone
concepts.explanation: A small electroacoustic transducer (moving-coil or balanced armature) that converts electrical signals into audible sound near the ear.

concepts.name: Photodiode
concepts.explanation: A light-sensitive semiconductor p–n junction diode that converts incident light into an electrical signal (current or voltage), operating via the photoelectric effect in a semiconductor.

concepts.name: AND gate
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs HIGH (1) only when all inputs are HIGH; implements logical conjunction.

concepts.name: OR gate
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs HIGH (1) when at least one input is HIGH; implements logical disjunction.

concepts.name: NOT gate (inverter)
concepts.explanation: A single-input digital logic gate that outputs the logical complement of its input; inverts the voltage level.

concepts.name: Newton's Second Law
concepts.explanation: The net force on a body equals its mass times acceleration (F = ma).

concepts.name: Equations of Motion with Constant Acceleration (SUVAT)
concepts.explanation: Kinematic relations for uniform acceleration, including v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at^2, and v^2 = u^2 + 2as.

concepts.name: Conservation of Linear Momentum
concepts.explanation: Total momentum of an isolated system remains constant during interactions (m1u1 + m2u2 = m1v1 + m2v2).

concepts.name: Linear Momentum
concepts.explanation: Momentum of a particle equals mass times velocity (p = mv).

concepts.name: Gravitational Potential Energy (near Earth's surface)
concepts.explanation: Potential energy of a mass in a uniform gravitational field, Ep = mgh.

concepts.name: Gravitational Field Strength from a Spherical Mass
concepts.explanation: Field strength at distance R from mass M: g = GM / R^2.

concepts.name: Orbital Period in a Central Gravitational Field
concepts.explanation: For circular orbits, T^2 = 4π^2 R^3 / GM.

concepts.name: Linear–Angular Speed Relationship
concepts.explanation: The tangential (linear) speed in circular motion equals radius times angular speed: v = rω.

concepts.name: Centripetal Acceleration
concepts.explanation: In uniform circular motion, a = v^2 / r = rω^2 directed toward the center.

concepts.name: Centripetal Force
concepts.explanation: Resultant inward force required for circular motion: F = mv^2 / r = m r ω^2.

concepts.name: Torque of a Couple
concepts.explanation: Forces of equal magnitude, opposite direction, and parallel lines of action produce a pure rotation with torque τ = Fd.

concepts.name: Hooke's Law
concepts.explanation: Restoring force in an ideal spring is proportional to extension and opposite in direction: F = −kx.

concepts.name: Simple Harmonic Motion Acceleration–Displacement Relation
concepts.explanation: In SHM, acceleration is proportional to and opposite the displacement: a = −ω^2 x.

concepts.name: Period, Frequency, and Angular Frequency Relations
concepts.explanation: Fundamental relations for oscillations: T = 1/f and ω = 2π/T.

concepts.name: Period of a Simple Pendulum
concepts.explanation: For small amplitudes, T = 2π √(l/g).

concepts.name: Hydrostatic Pressure
concepts.explanation: Pressure at depth in a fluid: p = ρ g h.

concepts.name: Addition and Subtraction Strategies
concepts.explanation: Using methods like making ten and decomposing numbers to add and subtract efficiently.

concepts.name: Decimal Operations
concepts.explanation: Adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing decimals with place-value reasoning.

concepts.name: Triangle Congruence
concepts.explanation: Establishing triangle equality using criteria such as SSS, SAS, ASA, and AAS.

concepts.name: Area, Perimeter, and Surface Area
concepts.explanation: Calculating boundary lengths and covering measures for 2D and 3D shapes.

concepts.name: Limits
concepts.explanation: Describing the behavior of functions as inputs approach specific values.

concepts.name: Derivatives
concepts.explanation: Measuring instantaneous rate of change and slopes of tangent lines.

concepts.name: Mathematical Induction
concepts.explanation: Proving statements for all integers by verifying a base case and an inductive step.

concepts.name: Logical Connectives
concepts.explanation: Using and, or, not, implication, and equivalence to build and analyze statements.

concepts.name: Celsius to Kelvin Conversion
concepts.explanation: The conversion between Celsius and Kelvin given by T(K) = T(°C) + 273.15, required for thermodynamic calculations in SI units.

concepts.name: Temperature Symbol Conventions (t in °C, T in K)
concepts.explanation: Standard notation where t denotes temperature measured in degrees Celsius (°C) and T denotes absolute temperature measured in kelvins (K).

concepts.name: Calorimetry Equation (Q = mcΔT)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative relationship linking heat added or removed, mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change.

concepts.name: Phase Change Energy Equation (Q = mL)
concepts.explanation: Calculates the heat required for a phase change using the mass and the specific latent heat for the process.

concepts.name: Specific Heat Capacity Formula (Q = m c Δθ)
concepts.explanation: Relates thermal energy transfer to mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change; valid when no phase change occurs and c is approximately constant.

concepts.name: Heat Capacity Formula (Q = C Δθ)
concepts.explanation: States that the heat added to a body equals its heat capacity times the temperature change.

concepts.name: Latent Heat (Energy for Change of State)
concepts.explanation: The total heat energy absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature without a temperature rise.

concepts.name: Latent Heat Equation (Q = mL)
concepts.explanation: Formula to calculate the heat involved in a phase change: Q is heat energy, m is mass, and L is specific latent heat.

concepts.name: Thin Lens and Mirror Formula
concepts.explanation: Imaging equation 1/f = 1/u + 1/v for spherical mirrors and thin lenses using standard sign conventions.

concepts.name: Magnification in Geometrical Optics
concepts.explanation: Linear magnification m = v/u (and m = image height/object height) with sign conventions for images.

concepts.name: Power of a Thin Lens
concepts.explanation: Defines lens power P = 1/f (in dioptres), positive for converging and negative for diverging lenses.

concepts.name: Lenses in Contact: Power Addition
concepts.explanation: For thin lenses in contact, total power is additive: P_total = P1 + P2.

concepts.name: Refractive Index and Wave Speed
concepts.explanation: Relates refractive index to speeds in two media: n = c1/c2 (or absolute n = c/v for a medium).

concepts.name: Apparent Depth and Refractive Index
concepts.explanation: For plane surfaces, n = real depth / apparent depth, explaining image shift in water or glass.

concepts.name: Wave Speed Relationship
concepts.explanation: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength: v = fλ (often written c = fλ for light).

concepts.name: Fundamental Frequency of a Stretched String
concepts.explanation: Lowest resonant frequency f1 = (1/2L)√(T/μ) for a string fixed at both ends, where T is tension and μ is linear mass density.

concepts.name: Capacitance
concepts.explanation: Defines a capacitor's ability to store charge per potential difference: C = Q/V.

concepts.name: Parallel-Plate Capacitor Capacitance
concepts.explanation: Capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor: C = εA/d (ε = ε0εr).

concepts.name: Electrical Resistivity
concepts.explanation: Material property relating resistance to geometry: ρ = R A / L.

concepts.name: Magnetic force on a moving charge (F = qvB)
concepts.explanation: A charge q moving with speed v perpendicular to a magnetic field B experiences a force of magnitude F = qvB (general vector form F = q v × B), with direction from the right-hand rule.

concepts.name: Force on a current-carrying conductor (F = B I l)
concepts.explanation: A straight conductor of length l carrying current I in a magnetic field B experiences a force F = B I l sinθ; direction by Fleming’s left-hand rule.

concepts.name: Magnetic flux (Φ = BA cosθ)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic flux Φ through area A at angle θ to a uniform field B is Φ = BA cosθ; it links magnetic fields to induced emf and is measured in webers.

concepts.name: RMS values of AC voltage and current
concepts.explanation: For sinusoidal waveforms, Vrms = V0/√2 and Irms = I0/√2; RMS gives the DC-equivalent values for power calculations, with P = Vrms Irms in resistive loads.

concepts.name: Transformer turns and voltage ratio
concepts.explanation: In an ideal transformer, the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio: Vp/Vs = Np/Ns; currents scale inversely and power is approximately conserved.

concepts.name: Electrical power in circuits (P = VI)
concepts.explanation: Electrical power is the rate of energy transfer: P = VI; for resistors, P can also be written as I^2R or V^2/R.

concepts.name: Joule’s law of heating (W = I^2 R t)
concepts.explanation: The thermal energy produced in a resistor over time t by current I is W = I^2 R t; forms the basis of electrical heating and power loss analyses.

concepts.name: Wheatstone bridge for resistance measurement
concepts.explanation: A bridge network used to determine an unknown resistance by balancing two legs of a circuit; at balance, R1/R2 = R3/Rx and galvanometer current is zero.

concepts.name: Einstein’s photoelectric equation
concepts.explanation: Relates photon energy to the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons: hf = Φ + 1/2 m v_max^2, establishing light quantization and threshold behavior.

concepts.name: Photon energy (E = hf)
concepts.explanation: The energy of a photon is proportional to frequency with Planck’s constant as the proportionality factor.

concepts.name: Work function (Φ)
concepts.explanation: The minimum energy required to liberate an electron from a material’s surface in the photoelectric effect.

concepts.name: Radioactive decay law
concepts.explanation: The rate of decay is proportional to the number of nuclei present: dN/dt = -λN, leading to exponential decay.

concepts.name: Half-life relation (T1/2 = ln 2 / λ)
concepts.explanation: Connects the half-life of a radionuclide to its decay constant, enabling determination of decay timescales.

concepts.name: Fractions on the Number Line
concepts.explanation: Representing fractions as points and lengths on a number line to show size and equivalence.

concepts.name: Laws of Exponents
concepts.explanation: Applying product, quotient, power, zero, and negative exponent rules to simplify expressions.

concepts.name: Descriptive Statistics: Mean and Standard Deviation
concepts.explanation: Measuring center and spread of data, computing and interpreting mean and standard deviation in context.

concepts.name: Adding Fractions with Unlike Denominators
concepts.explanation: Find a common denominator, convert each fraction to an equivalent form, then add numerators and simplify.

concepts.name: Linear Functions and Graphs
concepts.explanation: Model relationships with y = m*x + b, interpret slope and intercepts, and represent with tables, graphs, and equations.

concepts.name: Circumference and Area of Circles
concepts.explanation: Use C = 2*pi*r and A = pi*r^2 to measure circular distance and region; relate linear and quadratic growth.

concepts.name: Measures of Center and Spread
concepts.explanation: Summarize data with mean, median, and mode, and describe variability with range, IQR, and standard deviation.

concepts.name: Factoring Quadratic Expressions
concepts.explanation: Rewrite ax^2 + bx + c as a product of binomials or use special patterns to simplify and solve equations.

concepts.name: Quadratic Functions and Parabolas
concepts.explanation: Analyze y = a*x^2 + b*x + c in vertex, standard, or factored form to interpret features like vertex, axis, and zeros.

concepts.name: Systematic Error
concepts.explanation: A bias in measurement that shifts all results consistently above or below the true value due to calibration, method, or design flaws.

concepts.name: Random Error
concepts.explanation: Unpredictable measurement fluctuations that scatter results around the true value and can be reduced by repetition and averaging.

concepts.name: Accuracy
concepts.explanation: How close a measured value is to the true value; improved by eliminating systematic error.

concepts.name: Precision
concepts.explanation: How closely repeated measurements agree with each other; affected by random error.

concepts.name: Percentage Error
concepts.explanation: A normalized measure of error expressed as (error/true value)×100% or (estimated error/measured value)×100% when the true value is unknown.

concepts.name: Significant Figures
concepts.explanation: Rules for recording and rounding measured numbers to reflect measurement precision and propagate it through calculations.

concepts.name: Scientific Notation
concepts.explanation: Representing numbers as a×10^n (1 ≤ a < 10) to handle very large or small quantities efficiently.

concepts.name: Order of Magnitude Estimation
concepts.explanation: Estimating values by powers of ten and performing approximate calculations by rounding to one significant digit.

concepts.name: SI Base Units
concepts.explanation: The fundamental units (metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin) from which all other units are derived.

concepts.name: Derived Units
concepts.explanation: Units formed from products or quotients of base units, such as m s^-1 for speed or kg m^-3 for density.

concepts.name: Dimensional Analysis
concepts.explanation: Expressing quantities in base units to check consistency, derive units, and validate the plausibility of equations.

concepts.name: Dimensional Consistency of Equations
concepts.explanation: The requirement that all additive terms in a physical equation share identical units on both sides.

concepts.name: SI Unit Prefixes
concepts.explanation: Standard decimal prefixes (e.g., kilo, milli, micro, nano) used to represent multiples and submultiples of SI units.

concepts.name: Estimating Uncertainty from Instrument Resolution
concepts.explanation: Taking half the smallest scale division as the typical measurement uncertainty for many analog instruments.

concepts.name: Repeatability
concepts.explanation: The ability of the same observer using the same method to obtain the same results under identical conditions.

concepts.name: Reproducibility
concepts.explanation: The ability of different observers in different settings to obtain the same results using the same procedure.

concepts.name: Calibration of Instruments
concepts.explanation: Adjusting measurement devices to known standards to remove systematic offsets and improve accuracy.

concepts.name: Parallax Error
concepts.explanation: A reading error caused by viewing a scale from an angle; reduced by aligning the eye perpendicularly to the scale.

concepts.name: SI Unit Usage Conventions
concepts.explanation: Rules for writing and converting units, including spacing, capitalization, and consistent use of base units in calculations.

concepts.name: Scientific Method
concepts.explanation: The iterative process of questioning, modeling, predicting, experimenting, analyzing, and communicating to build scientific knowledge.

concepts.name: Models in Physics
concepts.explanation: Simplified representations based on assumptions that can be tested, refined, and used to make predictions.

concepts.name: Reflection of Light
concepts.explanation: Bouncing of light from a surface; part of incident light is returned from the surface.

concepts.name: Laws of Reflection of Light
concepts.explanation: For specular reflection: (1) incident ray, normal, and reflected ray lie in the same plane; (2) angle of incidence equals angle of reflection (i = r).

concepts.name: Ray Diagram Construction for Reflection
concepts.explanation: Procedure to model reflection: draw surface, normal at point of incidence, incident ray, and reflected ray with equal angles to the normal.

concepts.name: Plane Mirror Image Formation
concepts.explanation: A point object's image appears behind a plane mirror at the same perpendicular distance as the object, formed by apparent intersection of reflected rays.

concepts.name: Virtual Image
concepts.explanation: An image formed by apparent intersection of rays; no light actually passes through the image location (e.g., plane mirror images).

concepts.name: Regular (Specular) Reflection
concepts.explanation: Mirror-like reflection from a smooth surface where reflected rays are orderly and obey the laws of reflection.

concepts.name: Diffuse Reflection
concepts.explanation: Scattering of reflected light in many directions from a rough or matte surface, allowing objects to be seen from multiple viewing angles.

concepts.name: Normal at the Point of Incidence
concepts.explanation: A line drawn perpendicular to the reflecting surface at the point where the incident ray strikes; used as reference for measuring angles.

concepts.name: Angle of Incidence
concepts.explanation: The angle between the incident ray and the normal at the point of incidence.

concepts.name: Angle of Reflection
concepts.explanation: The angle between the reflected ray and the normal; equal to the angle of incidence for specular reflection.

concepts.name: Incident Ray
concepts.explanation: The incoming ray that strikes a reflective surface at the point of incidence.

concepts.name: Reflected Ray
concepts.explanation: The ray that leaves the surface after reflection, making an angle with the normal equal to the angle of incidence for specular reflection.

concepts.name: Light Travels in Straight Lines
concepts.explanation: In uniform media, light propagates along straight-line paths (rectilinear propagation), forming the basis for ray models and shadows.

concepts.name: Light Ray (Ray Model of Light)
concepts.explanation: An idealized line indicating the direction of light propagation used to analyze reflection and image formation.

concepts.name: Parallel Beam of Light
concepts.explanation: A bundle of rays that remain at constant separation; often produced by lasers or collimated sources.

concepts.name: Converging Beam of Light
concepts.explanation: A bundle of rays whose separation decreases along propagation, tending toward a focal point.

concepts.name: Diverging Beam of Light
concepts.explanation: A bundle of rays whose separation increases along propagation, spreading out from a point or region.

concepts.name: Luminous Object
concepts.explanation: An object that emits its own light (e.g., Sun, stars, a lit LED), enabling direct visibility.

concepts.name: Non-Luminous Object
concepts.explanation: An object that does not emit light; visible only by reflecting light from other sources.

concepts.name: Visible Light
concepts.explanation: The portion of electromagnetic radiation detectable by the human eye; required for vision as light must enter the eye from objects to be seen.

concepts.name: Speed of Light
concepts.explanation: Light travels in vacuum at approximately 3.0 × 10^8 m/s; its finiteness allows time-of-travel calculations.

concepts.name: Light-Year
concepts.explanation: A unit of distance equal to the distance light travels in one year in vacuum.

concepts.name: Reversibility (Ray Retracing) of Light
concepts.explanation: A light ray will retrace its path if its direction is reversed; follows from equality of incidence and reflection angles.

concepts.name: Reflection from Perpendicular Plane Mirrors
concepts.explanation: A ray reflecting sequentially from two perpendicular plane mirrors changes direction by 90 degrees, with equal incidence and reflection at each surface.

concepts.name: Demonstration: Straight-Line Propagation of Light
concepts.explanation: Three-card holes alignment experiment showing that light passes through only when holes are collinear, evidencing rectilinear propagation.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of the Laws of Reflection
concepts.explanation: Ray box and mirror method using a protractor to measure i and r and to confirm i = r and coplanarity of rays and normal.

concepts.name: Lateral Inversion in Plane Mirrors
concepts.explanation: Left-right reversal of images in a plane mirror relative to the object’s front-back axis, a property of virtual images from plane mirrors.

concepts.name: Apparent Size and Visual Angle
concepts.explanation: Perceived size of an object is determined by the angular separation of rays from its top and bottom at the eye (visual angle).

concepts.name: Refraction of Light
concepts.explanation: Bending of light when it passes between media with different refractive indices due to a change in speed; no bending at normal incidence or if indices are equal.

concepts.name: Snell's Law
concepts.explanation: The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for two media: sin i / sin r = n.

concepts.name: First Law of Refraction
concepts.explanation: The incident ray, the normal at the point of incidence, and the refracted ray all lie in the same plane.

concepts.name: Refractive Index of a Medium
concepts.explanation: For light from vacuum/air into a medium, n = sin i / sin r; n ≥ 1 and indicates how strongly the medium bends light.

concepts.name: Refractive Index Between Two Media
concepts.explanation: For light traveling from medium x to y, n_xy = sin i / sin r; indices are reciprocal: n_xy = 1 / n_yx.

concepts.name: Refractive Index in Terms of Relative Speeds
concepts.explanation: For light passing from medium 1 to 2, sin i / sin r = c1 / c2; relative to air, n = c_air / c_medium.

concepts.name: Direction of Refraction and Optical Density
concepts.explanation: Light bends toward the normal entering an optically denser medium and away from the normal entering an optically rarer medium; optical density differs from physical density.

concepts.name: Conditions for No Refraction
concepts.explanation: No bending occurs if the ray is incident along the normal, or if the two media have equal refractive indices (equal light speeds).

concepts.name: Refractive Index–Critical Angle Relationship
concepts.explanation: For a medium bordered by air, n = 1 / sin C; equivalently sin C = 1/n.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of Snell's Law (Ray Box and Glass Block)
concepts.explanation: Measure i and r for multiple incidences on a rectangular block, compute sin i / sin r, and plot sin i vs sin r; constant ratio and slope give the refractive index.

concepts.name: Measuring the Critical Angle with a Semicircular Block
concepts.explanation: Increase the incidence angle until the refracted ray skims the flat face; measure C and verify n = 1/sin C.

concepts.name: Apparent Depth and Virtual Image in Refraction
concepts.explanation: An object viewed from air into water appears shallower due to refraction; observer sees a virtual image closer to the surface.

concepts.name: Right-Angle Prism as 90°/180° Reflector via TIR
concepts.explanation: A 45°–90°–45° prism produces total internal reflection at 45° if C < 45°, turning beams by 90° or 180°; requires n > 1/ sin 45° ≈ 1.414.

concepts.name: Optical Fibre Principle
concepts.explanation: A thin transparent core guides light by repeated total internal reflection when the incidence at the core–cladding boundary exceeds the critical angle.

concepts.name: Optical Fibre Cladding and Loss Mechanisms
concepts.explanation: Light can escape due to excessive bending or contact between fibres; cladding with lower refractive index maintains TIR and reduces coupling losses.

concepts.name: Corner Cube Retroreflector
concepts.explanation: Three mutually perpendicular reflecting faces (or prisms) return incident light parallel to its incoming direction via multiple TIR, used in safety reflectors.

concepts.name: Cat's-Eye Reflector
concepts.explanation: A road reflector that returns headlights via total internal reflection within a transparent element.

concepts.name: Snell's Window
concepts.explanation: Underwater observers see a circular 'window' of the above-world defined by the critical angle; radius at the surface r = depth × tan C.

concepts.name: Sign conventions for thin lens equation
concepts.explanation: u is taken positive; v is positive for real images and negative for virtual images; f is positive for converging lenses and negative for diverging lenses. These conventions determine the image nature from the equation.

concepts.name: Converging lens (convex lens)
concepts.explanation: A lens thicker at the center than the edges that refracts a parallel beam to a focus, turning it into a converging beam; can form real or virtual images depending on object position.

concepts.name: Diverging lens (concave lens)
concepts.explanation: A lens thinner at the center than the edges that refracts a parallel beam so it appears to diverge from a focus; always forms a virtual, upright, diminished image on the same side as the object.

concepts.name: Principal focus (focal point) of a lens
concepts.explanation: For rays parallel to the principal axis, the point where a converging lens brings them together or from which a diverging lens appears to spread them; each lens has two symmetric foci.

concepts.name: Focal length of a lens
concepts.explanation: Distance from the optic centre to the principal focus; shorter focal length implies stronger converging or diverging effect.

concepts.name: Principal axis of a lens
concepts.explanation: The straight line through the optic centre perpendicular to the lens surfaces; used as the reference line in ray diagrams.

concepts.name: Optic centre of a lens
concepts.explanation: The central point of a thin lens through which a ray passes undeviated; used as the origin for measuring u and v.

concepts.name: Principal ray rules for a converging lens
concepts.explanation: Three construction rays: (1) through the optic centre goes straight; (2) parallel to axis refracts through far focus; (3) through near focus emerges parallel to axis.

concepts.name: Ray diagram construction for converging lenses
concepts.explanation: Skill of drawing any two principal rays from a point on the object to locate the image position, orientation, and size.

concepts.name: Real image
concepts.explanation: An image formed by actual intersection of rays; can be projected on a screen and is typically inverted relative to the object.

concepts.name: Image characteristics vs object distance for a converging lens
concepts.explanation: For object beyond 2f: real, inverted, diminished; at 2f: real, inverted, same size; between f and 2f: real, inverted, magnified; at f: image at infinity; inside f: virtual, upright, magnified on same side.

concepts.name: Simple magnifier (magnifying glass) operation
concepts.explanation: Placing the object inside the focal length of a converging lens produces an upright, virtual, magnified image used for visual magnification.

concepts.name: Image of a distant object in a converging lens
concepts.explanation: Light from an object at practical infinity arrives as parallel rays and forms a real image at the focus (on the focal plane), small and inverted.

concepts.name: Focal plane
concepts.explanation: The plane perpendicular to the principal axis that passes through the focus; images of distant scenes form on this plane.

concepts.name: Image formation in a diverging lens
concepts.explanation: A diverging lens always forms a virtual, upright, diminished image on the same side as the object; image size increases as the object moves closer but remains diminished.

concepts.name: Experimental verification of the thin lens equation
concepts.explanation: Lab procedure: form real images of an illuminated object on a screen, measure u and v from the optic centre, compute 1/u + 1/v and deduce f; repeat for multiple trials to confirm the model.

concepts.name: Graphical determination of focal length (1/u vs 1/v plot)
concepts.explanation: Plot 1/u against 1/v for measured pairs; the straight-line intercepts on the axes give 1/f, whose average yields the focal length.

concepts.name: Sources of error in lens experiments
concepts.explanation: Uncertainty in focus judgment, measuring from the true optic centre, and parallax when reading scales; can introduce random or systematic errors.

concepts.name: Two-position method for fixed object–screen distance (lens displacement)
concepts.explanation: For a fixed separation of object and screen greater than 4f, there are two lens positions producing sharp images; the separation of lens positions relates to focal length and can be used to find f.

concepts.name: Correction of myopia (short-sight) with a diverging lens
concepts.explanation: A diverging lens pre-diverges incoming rays so the eye’s optics can focus distant objects onto the retina; implemented as distance glasses.

concepts.name: Correction of hyperopia (long-sight) with a converging lens
concepts.explanation: A converging lens pre-converges light from near objects so the eye focuses the image on the retina; implemented as reading glasses.

concepts.name: Camera image formation with a converging lens
concepts.explanation: A converging lens forms a real image on a film or sensor plane; focusing adjusts the image distance to achieve sharpness on the sensor.

concepts.name: Compound microscope image formation
concepts.explanation: The objective forms a real, magnified intermediate image; the eyepiece (a magnifier) then produces a further magnified virtual image for the observer.

concepts.name: Astronomical telescope (refracting) image formation
concepts.explanation: The objective lens forms a real image of a distant object at its focal plane; the eyepiece acts as a magnifying glass to produce an enlarged virtual image.

concepts.name: Geometrical optics (ray model of light)
concepts.explanation: Model assuming light travels in straight rays and obeys reflection and refraction laws; effective for predicting lens and mirror behavior but breaks down at very small scales.

concepts.name: Average Speed
concepts.explanation: Total distance divided by total time for a motion segment: v = s/t or Δs/Δt.

concepts.name: Instantaneous Speed
concepts.explanation: Speed at a specific instant; approximated by measuring average speed over a very short time or small distance.

concepts.name: Average Velocity
concepts.explanation: Displacement divided by time: v_avg = Δs/Δt; includes magnitude and direction.

concepts.name: Instantaneous Velocity
concepts.explanation: Velocity at a particular instant; equals the slope of the displacement-time graph at that point and can be approximated by average velocity over a very short interval.

concepts.name: Constant Speed
concepts.explanation: Speed that does not change; average speed is the same over any segment of the motion.

concepts.name: Constant Velocity
concepts.explanation: Motion with unchanging speed and direction; no speeding up, slowing down, or turning.

concepts.name: Constant (Uniform) Acceleration
concepts.explanation: Acceleration that remains the same over time so that average acceleration is identical across any interval.

concepts.name: Kinematic Equations (Constant Acceleration)
concepts.explanation: Relations for straight-line motion with constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + 1/2 at^2; v^2 = u^2 + 2as.

concepts.name: Displacement-Time Graph: Slope Equals Velocity
concepts.explanation: For one-dimensional motion, the slope (rise/run) of an s–t graph gives the velocity; straight line implies constant velocity.

concepts.name: Tangent Method for Instantaneous Velocity
concepts.explanation: For a curved displacement-time graph, the slope of the tangent at a point gives instantaneous velocity at that time.

concepts.name: Velocity-Time Graph: Slope Equals Acceleration
concepts.explanation: The slope of a v–t graph gives acceleration; straight line indicates constant acceleration.

concepts.name: Area Under Velocity-Time Graph
concepts.explanation: The area between the v–t curve and the time axis equals the displacement (or distance for speed-time).

concepts.name: Sign Convention in One-Dimensional Motion
concepts.explanation: Assigning positive direction (e.g., right/east) so that displacement and velocity to the opposite direction are negative.

concepts.name: Measuring Velocity with Ticker Timer and Ticker Tape
concepts.explanation: Using a 50 Hz timer to produce dots on tape; evenly spaced dots indicate constant velocity; compute v from distance between dots and time per space.

concepts.name: Measuring Velocity with Light Gate and Scaler Timer
concepts.explanation: Passing a card of known length through a light gate to measure transit time and compute near-instantaneous velocity v = l/t.

concepts.name: Linear Air Track (Friction Reduction for Constant Velocity)
concepts.explanation: Device that levitates a rider on air to minimize friction, enabling near-constant velocity motion for precise measurements.

concepts.name: Measuring Constant Acceleration with Ticker Tape
concepts.explanation: Use increasing spacing of dots to determine u and v over short segments and compute a = (v − u)/t between reference marks.

concepts.name: Measuring Acceleration with Two Light Gates
concepts.explanation: Measure initial and final velocities with two gates and known separation s to compute a = (v^2 − u^2)/(2s).

concepts.name: Acceleration Due to Gravity (g)
concepts.explanation: Constant downward acceleration near Earth’s surface (≈9.8 m s^-2), same for all objects neglecting air resistance.

concepts.name: Measuring g with Free-Fall Apparatus
concepts.explanation: Drop a steel ball, measure fall time over distance s, use s = 1/2 g t^2 or slope of s vs t^2 (g = 2 × slope) to determine g.

concepts.name: Distance vs Displacement; Scalar vs Vector
concepts.explanation: Distance and speed are scalars; displacement and velocity are vectors that include direction; essential distinction in kinematics.

concepts.name: Deceleration (Negative Acceleration)
concepts.explanation: A decrease in speed represented by acceleration with a negative sign relative to chosen positive direction.

concepts.name: Unit Conversion Between km h^-1 and m s^-1
concepts.explanation: Convert speeds: 1 km h^-1 = 0.277... m s^-1; necessary for consistent SI calculations in kinematics.

concepts.name: Parallax Error Avoidance in Length Measurement
concepts.explanation: Align eye perpendicularly to scale when using metre sticks or calipers to reduce systematic error in distance measurements.

concepts.name: Compensating Runway for Friction to Achieve Constant Velocity
concepts.explanation: Slightly incline the runway to balance rolling friction so a pushed trolley moves with constant velocity (verified by equal tape spacing).

concepts.name: Using Data Logger and Motion Sensor for Kinematics Graphs
concepts.explanation: Collect real-time position or velocity data to plot s–t or v–t graphs and compute slopes for speed or acceleration.

concepts.name: Vector Quantity
concepts.explanation: A physical quantity that has both magnitude and direction and must be specified by both to be fully described.

concepts.name: Scalar Quantity
concepts.explanation: A physical quantity with magnitude only and no direction; combined by ordinary arithmetic.

concepts.name: Resultant of Two Vectors
concepts.explanation: The single vector that has the same effect as two given vectors acting together; also called the net vector.

concepts.name: Parallelogram Law of Vector Addition
concepts.explanation: When two vectors are drawn from a common tail as adjacent sides of a parallelogram, the diagonal from the common tail gives the resultant.

concepts.name: Triangle Law of Vector Addition
concepts.explanation: When two vectors are placed head-to-tail, the vector from the tail of the first to the head of the second is the resultant.

concepts.name: Vector Addition in One Dimension
concepts.explanation: For collinear vectors, add magnitudes for the same direction; use a sign convention to subtract when directions are opposite; the resultant direction follows the larger magnitude.

concepts.name: Resolving a Vector into Perpendicular Components
concepts.explanation: Expressing a vector as the sum of two perpendicular vectors (components), each representing the full effect along its direction.

concepts.name: Component Formulas for Perpendicular Resolution
concepts.explanation: If a vector of magnitude v makes angle θ with the x-component, the components are x = v cos θ and y = v sin θ.

concepts.name: Graphical Representation of Vectors
concepts.explanation: Vectors are represented by arrows on diagrams; arrow length is proportional to magnitude and arrow direction gives the vector direction.

concepts.name: Net Force
concepts.explanation: The single force equivalent to the combined effect of all forces acting on an object; determines the object's acceleration.

concepts.name: Equilibrium of Three Concurrent Forces
concepts.explanation: If three forces keep a particle at rest, the resultant of any two is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the third.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of Vector Addition in Two Dimensions
concepts.explanation: Using a force table with pulleys, threads, and weights to set a knot in equilibrium; the diagonal of the parallelogram equals the resultant and is equal and opposite to the third force.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of Vector Addition in One Dimension
concepts.explanation: Using spring balances and a trolley to show that equal and opposite forces yield zero resultant and that the sum of collinear forces in one direction equals the opposing force at equilibrium.

concepts.name: Determining Resultant Using Pythagoras and Trigonometry
concepts.explanation: For perpendicular vectors, the resultant magnitude is found with Pythagoras and the direction with inverse tangent of the component ratio.

concepts.name: Newton's Second Law of Motion
concepts.explanation: The net force on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum and, for constant mass, F_net = m a.

concepts.name: Force equals mass times acceleration (F = m a)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative form of Newton’s second law relating net force, mass, and acceleration.

concepts.name: Momentum (p = m v)
concepts.explanation: A vector quantity equal to mass times velocity; SI unit kg m s^-1.

concepts.name: Newton's First Law of Motion (Inertia)
concepts.explanation: A body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted on by a net external force.

concepts.name: Newton's Third Law of Motion (Action–Reaction)
concepts.explanation: For every action force on one body, there is an equal and opposite reaction force on another body.

concepts.name: Projectile Motion (Oblique Launch)
concepts.explanation: Two-dimensional motion under gravity with independent horizontal constant velocity and vertical constant acceleration components.

concepts.name: Projectile Motion (Horizontal Launch)
concepts.explanation: Motion of an object launched horizontally: horizontal speed constant; vertical motion identical to free fall.

concepts.name: Weight (W = m g)
concepts.explanation: The gravitational force on a mass near Earth; proportional to mass and local gravitational acceleration.

concepts.name: Net (Resultant) Force
concepts.explanation: Vector sum of all external forces on a body; determines the body’s acceleration via F_net = m a.

concepts.name: Force as a Vector Quantity
concepts.explanation: Force has magnitude and direction; represented by F and measured in newtons (N).

concepts.name: Mass (Inertial Mass)
concepts.explanation: A scalar measure of the amount of matter and of resistance to acceleration; SI unit kilogram.

concepts.name: Frictional Force
concepts.explanation: A contact force that opposes relative motion between surfaces; can prevent or reduce motion.

concepts.name: Air Resistance (Drag)
concepts.explanation: A resistive force opposing motion through air, increasing with speed and cross-sectional area, dependent on shape.

concepts.name: Terminal Velocity
concepts.explanation: Steady falling speed reached when upward air resistance equals weight, giving zero net force.

concepts.name: Normal Reaction Force
concepts.explanation: Perpendicular contact force exerted by a surface supporting an object.

concepts.name: Tension Force
concepts.explanation: Pulling force transmitted through a string, rope, or cable along its length.

concepts.name: Centre of Mass
concepts.explanation: Point where the mass distribution can be considered concentrated for translational motion; forces through it cause no rotation.

concepts.name: Acceleration of the Centre of Mass
concepts.explanation: The centre of mass accelerates according to F_net = m a_cm for a system of particles or a rigid body.

concepts.name: Centre of Gravity
concepts.explanation: Point through which the entire weight of a body acts; coincides with centre of mass in uniform gravitational fields.

concepts.name: Conservation of Momentum in Two Dimensions
concepts.explanation: Momentum components are conserved independently along perpendicular axes in isolated collisions.

concepts.name: Rocket Propulsion via Conservation of Momentum
concepts.explanation: Expelling mass generates equal and opposite momentum change, accelerating the rocket.

concepts.name: Definition of the Newton (N)
concepts.explanation: One newton is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m s^-2 (1 N = 1 kg m s^-2).

concepts.name: Acceleration Proportional to Net Force
concepts.explanation: For a given mass, acceleration increases directly with the applied net force (a ∝ F).

concepts.name: Acceleration Inversely Proportional to Mass
concepts.explanation: For a fixed net force, acceleration decreases as mass increases (a ∝ 1/m).

concepts.name: Pressure (P = F/A)
concepts.explanation: Pressure is the force acting uniformly per unit area on a surface: P = F/A. It is a scalar and its SI unit is the pascal (Pa).

concepts.name: Hydrostatic Pressure in a Liquid (P = ρgh)
concepts.explanation: The pressure difference between two depths in a liquid of density ρ is P = ρgh, increasing linearly with depth.

concepts.name: Buoyancy Force (Upthrust)
concepts.explanation: An object immersed in a fluid experiences a net upward force due to higher pressure at greater depths; this is the buoyancy force (upthrust).

concepts.name: Floating Equilibrium Condition
concepts.explanation: For a floating object, the buoyancy force on the submerged portion equals the object's weight, resulting in zero vertical acceleration.

concepts.name: Absolute Pressure in a Fluid (P_abs = P_atm + ρgh)
concepts.explanation: When a fluid is exposed to the atmosphere, the absolute pressure at depth h is the sum of atmospheric pressure and hydrostatic pressure: P_abs = P_atm + ρgh.

concepts.name: Atmospheric Pressure
concepts.explanation: The atmosphere exerts pressure on surfaces, typically about 1.0×10^5 Pa at sea level, decreasing with altitude and measurable with a barometer.

concepts.name: Weight and Acceleration Due to Gravity (W = mg)
concepts.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force on a mass near a planet’s surface, given by W = mg, where g is local gravitational field strength.

concepts.name: Acceleration Due to Gravity Near a Planet (g = GM/R^2)
concepts.explanation: At a planet’s surface, acceleration due to gravity is g = GM/R^2, depending on the planet’s mass M and radius R.

concepts.name: Gravitational Field Strength (g = F/m)
